People Business Partner, GTM at LiveKit

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing.
  • We're looking for a Senior People Business Partner for our GTM org.
  • Industry observers note that you build the kind of relationships where leaders and individual contributors bring you the hard stuff while there's still time to proactively do something about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

We're looking for a Senior People Business Partner for our GTM org. You don't need to be the deep expert in every corner, but you're dangerous enough across all of it to move fast and recognize when something deserves more attention than you can give it right now. You also know when to slow down and when to raise the harder question early.

Industry observers note that you build the kind of relationships where leaders and individual contributors bring you the hard stuff while there's still time to proactively do something about it. You're approachable, direct, and willing to push back when something doesn't make sense. You don't need every answer, but you know how to ask good questions, work through messy situations, and help leaders make better decisions.

You'll partner with leaders across Sales, Marketing, and the rest of our revenue organization as they build and grow their teams, and you'll work closely with our VP of People and the broader People team to build scalable, intentional People programs that enable folks to do their best work.

You'll thrive as a People Business Partner if you:.

Take the time to understand the business just as much as the people side.

Have worked in enough different environments to have a real sense of what good looks like, and hold yourself to it.

Stay steady when a sales org is moving fast: quota changes, reorgs, and rapid hiring don't rattle you.

Are direct with people, including when it's uncomfortable—feedback doesn't get softened into confusion, and people still trust you after.

Assess risk quickly—not just what could go wrong, but what's actually likely to and how much it matters.

Know when to escalate and when to just decide; you bring a recommendation, not just a problem, and you know which things (comp exceptions, anything legal, changes to established policy) always get a second set of eyes.

As a People Business Partner at LiveKit, you will:.

Own performance management, manager coaching, org design, and headcount planning as the primary People partner for Sales, Marketing, and our broader Revenue organization, including pre- and post-sales teams.

Navigate complex situations and help the org grow without breaking, including pushing back on adding layers or headcount before the case is made.

Partner with our GTM Talent Partner on hiring prepares, role scoping, and ramp so headcount decisions are made with the full picture.

Work as one team with the other People Business Partners (EPD and G&A) so leaders get a consistent partnership experience.

Work directly with the VP of People and larger People and Talent team to design, build, and operationalize People programs across all COEs.

Own end-to-end delivery of programs and projects, from strategy to rollout to iteration.

Make our work repeatable: documented, handoff-ready, and not dependent on anyone being a hero.

Experience as a People Business Partner (or equivalent) supporting Sales and other revenue-generating teams: performance management against quota and ramp, comp strategy changes, rev org reorgs, and coaching sales managers.

Think from first principles and know when to ask for help.

A clear, direct communicator who can challenge strong personalities while maintaining trust.

Confident in what you know and what you don't—able to respond decisively even without full information.

Comfortable in ambiguity, with strong relationship-building instincts and data-informed decision-making.

Personable, approachable, and comfortable working with leaders and ICs at all levels.

Understand how hiring, talent development, and organizational decisions impact a sales team's success.

Experience with global HR, leaves of absence, or benefits administration.

Direct experience building or significantly iterating programs across multiple People COEs.

Experience using AI tools to improve how you work, with good judgment about when and how to use them.

An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

Work alongside world-class people at one of the most vital AI infrastructure companies being built right now.

Competitive salary and equity package.

Health, dental, and vision benefits.

LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

Senior Software Engineer II, Agentic Apps at Kit

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love.
  • Creators use Kit's first-party apps and integrations to connect Kit to the rest of their business.
  • You'll be the first engineer on the Apps squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

Creators use Kit's first-party apps and integrations to connect Kit to the rest of their business. Today we build and maintain these apps by hand, with help from an agency partner. That doesn't scale. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer II to own app delivery and maintenance end to end, so a small team can support creators of every size.

You'll be the first engineer on the Apps squad. Your focus is shipping high quality apps at a high pace, and maintaining them to an industry-best standard. To get there, you'll take a systems-level view and build on Kit's coding agent. You'll work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad, which builds the coding agent. You'll own the creator experience of every app you build, and you're free to improve Kit's platform when that makes those apps better.

According to recent reports, this is a full-time IC role for an AI-first, product-minded, full-stack engineer who has shipped agent workflows to production and judges them by reliable outcomes, not lines of code. You combine technical depth with leadership and extreme ownership. You take input from Partnerships, Product, and Design to help shape the "what," and you own the "how." You thrive in ambiguity, take initiative without waiting for permission, and elevate everyone around you through your generosity and optimism.

We're excited about first-party apps because they let creators do more with Kit than Kit does on its own. Our own apps should just work, and set the bar for every app built on Kit.

You'll report to John Bohannon, Senior Engineering Manager for the Ecosystem and Apps squads. You'll collaborate closely with a Partnerships Manager, Product Manager, Product Designer, and engineers on the Ecosystem squad. You'll also work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad on Kit's coding agent, and with a contractor who helps maintain our apps.

In a recent development, the Apps squad works as a sibling to Ecosystem. You'll set its rhythms, collaborate with our Partnerships Manager on which apps to build next, and join Ecosystem's cycle planning.

A peer onboarding buddy will help you learn our systems and codebase, and you'll have engineers across Kit for support and mentorship.

It has been revealed that first Week: Set up your local environment and merge your first production code. Meet the team through Get To Know You's. Start the app handover with the contractor who maintains them today. Watch the recorded app walkthroughs and read the runbooks for our most-used apps.

In a recent development, first Month: Audit our first-party apps and integrations, starting with the apps that need the most maintenance. Measure what each app costs to maintain, including partner app reviews like those at Google, Meta, and Shopify. Learn how Kit's API, OAuth, and App Store support creators from small to large. Fix bugs and support escalations in the apps you now own. Learn how Kit's coding agent works with the AI Developer Experience squad.

First Three Months: Adapt Kit's coding agent to build your first apps and maintain existing ones. Give it the context, guardrails, and evals it needs. Turn what you learn into shared pieces every app can use, like a reusable load test, infrastructure automation, and app manifests. Write runbooks that let others work on any app. Drive each app's maintenance toward zero human time with the coding agent.

First Six Months: Ship newly introduced apps at a steady pace. Take over the rest of the app catalog and apply the coding agent to its maintenance. Show that one engineer with agents can maintain many apps at high quality. Define the metrics and dashboards for agent-built apps: debuts, reliability, time to fix, and revenue impact. Share how agents build and maintain our apps, for example in a Lunch & Learn.

First Year: Kit ships more high-quality apps, faster, and the coding agent handles more of the routine builds and fixes, with you steering the system. The legacy integration model is retired. You use catalog metrics to recommend where the Apps squad invests next. You and the AI Developer Experience squad improve the coding agent together, so other Kit engineers benefit too.

Expert in agentic AI development. You've built agent workflows that ship and maintain production code, with evals, guardrails, and human review.

In a recent development, strong in APIs, including OAuth, webhooks, and integrations with third-party platforms. Fluent in Ruby on Rails, or able to ramp into it fast. Full-stack, with React where an app needs it.

Recent findings suggest that ship well-tested, performant, accessible code, whether you or an agent writes it. Set the quality bar and build the tests, evals, and reviews that hold agents to it.

Set up dashboards, alerts, and load tests that find problems across many apps early.

Measure each app's maintenance cost, and make the team's open capacity for latest apps easy to see.

Communicate clearly across Engineering, Product, Design, and Partnerships.

Align others on goals, trade-offs, and success criteria without formal authority.

Led a major cross-team initiative from ambiguous requirements to delivery, partnering with senior leaders across functions, with measurable business impact.

Built agents or tools that measurably improved how a team ships software, not only how much code it writes.

Took ownership of a codebase someone else built, with thin documentation, and made it maintainable.

Independently managed a large project, such as a migration or deprecation that required customers or partners to move.

Recent findings suggest that create leverage, not only features. Invest in reusable systems that make your team and others faster.

According to recent reports, judge AI work by outcomes, like releases and reliability, not by the volume of code or PRs. Share what works and what the risks are.

Own everything you and your agents produce, from code to PR descriptions. Know the details well enough to stand behind every line, and don't leave reviewers or readers to do the work.

Lead work without waiting for a formal role or permission.

Make reversible product decisions on your own, and know when to pull in cross-functional stakeholders like Product, Design, Partnerships, and Support.

Break big, ambiguous problems into steps that you and others can deliver.

Write docs that let others work on any app, so the work doesn't depend on one person.

Put creator outcomes ahead of features.

Recent findings suggest that share work in progress and the reasons behind trade-offs. Give and ask for direct feedback.

You will stand out if you have:.

Built AI tools that other developers use, such as MCP servers, agent skills, or eval suites.

Built integrations with creator-economy platforms.

Directed the work of contractors or an agency partner.

Shared your work through talks, blog posts, or open-source contributions.

Needing established processes, full consensus, or permission before you move forward.

Wanting a large team of engineering peers on your own team from day one.

Preferring to stay heads-down in code over shaping what to build with Partnerships, Product, and Design.

Preferring greenfield work over inheriting and improving legacy code.

Building each app by hand when a shared system could serve many.

Measuring AI success by code volume instead of shipped, reliable apps.

Avoiding direct feedback, whether giving or receiving it.

Industry observers note that we're 100% remote with team members across the globe. We work mostly on East Coast time—so if you're based on the West Coast of the United States, Europe, or Asia, you might have a few early mornings or late evenings. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

Industry observers note that kit has standardized salaries based on position, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re hiring at our level P4 ($186,000/year). Level is determined based on experience and our interview process.

Sources indicate that we cover up to $2,280 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance aims through Aetna.

$2,000 equipment allowance for your first two years, $1,000 budget every following two years. Organization-provided laptops are issued to every Kit team member and are not included in the equipment budget.

Individual learning + development budget ($3,500/year).

Creator meetup budget ($50/month) to connect with creators over coffee, lunch, or other in-person meetups.

Childcare benefit up to $3,000 annually through JOON.

Twenty (20) days of paid time off during each year of employment.

Paid paid vacation: An after-tax bonus of $1,000 for taking five consecutive days of vacation where you’re fully unplugged from work.

Two weeks of paid sick time each year, including mental health + well being days.

Twelve (12) weeks paid parental leave and flexible scheduling in your child’s first year.

Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months.

Sources indicate that winter Break Closure: Kit closes for a week at the end of December, giving everyone a collective break to enjoy the holiday season. Essential support services remain available, with teams coordinating to ensure coverage during this period.

Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team.

Fantastic in-person or virtual retreats with the team twice a year.

We usually receive a large number of applications, and our goal is to follow up with you within two weeks. You’ll hear from us either way. Here’s what you can expect from the rest of our hiring process:.

Phone screen with our recruiter (30 min).

Hiring manager interview (45 min).

Technical execution and leadership/collaboration interview (60 min).

We’ll keep you informed through every step. To get started, complete this application, including a cover letter and answers to the questions on the next page. We read every single application, and your cover letter and responses help put your experience into context.

Kit is an equal opportunity employer.

We value diversity in all of its forms. Research tells us that applicants who are female or non-binary, as well as applicants who are people of color, are less likely to apply for roles they do not feel 100% qualified for. If you think you meet more than 50% of our requirements but fewer than 100% of them, please apply.

We’re imperfect communicators, so think of our job postings as the starting point for discussion rather than proof that you shouldn’t apply.

Kit does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We’re looking for a Head of M&A to join our Corporate Development team and help build M&A from scratch. You’ll work closely with product, engineering, finance, legal, as well as founders we might acquire, helping us build a world class M&A team.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

From games like Transformers: Earth Wars, Rodeo Stampede and Ski Safari, to bringing iconic IPs from Hasbro, AMC, Netflix, Paramount and Sony Pictures to leading studios like Rivergame, Candivore, 37Games and Tencent Studios, we connect creativity with global expertise.

    It has been revealed that our work spans game development, publishing, IP licensing and ad monetization across mobile, PC and console. We build games, grow franchises and help developers reach players worldwide. We love games. We play games. And together, we grow games that last.

    We believe in the power of games and that everyone deserves the opportunity to build a life they love, from anywhere in the world.

    We're fully remote by design. We embrace Work From Anywhere, with no fixed hours or limits on time off. We trust our people to own their work and deliver results.

    Industry observers note that we're driven by performance, curiosity, and continuous improvement. We experiment often, challenge assumptions and value impact over titles.

    Recent findings suggest that yodo1 is looking for an Art Manager to lead our in-house Creative Services team and turn it into the go-to art partner for our game studios, our PC publishing label Spicy Koala and our marketing team. You will sit between the people who need art and the people who make it: understand what each team needs, plan how and when it gets delivered, decide whether it is made in-house or outsourced, and make sure it ships on time, on budget and on brand.

    Focused on impact. You understand the 80/20 rule and focus on activities that matter.

    It has been revealed that performance-driven and growth-oriented. You have an intrinsic will to succeed while unafraid to try, fail, and learn by experimenting with new approaches and testing ideas.

    It has been revealed that cooperative. You help others succeed; you give and receive feedback well.

    Sources indicate that relentlessly curious. You ask questions.

    Sources indicate that humble. You ask for help; you are quick to admit and learn from your mistakes.

    SMART. You work and communicate in ways that are Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Relevant, and Time-bound.

    Lead and manage the Creative Services team as the single point of contact for all art, video and creative requests.

    Assess the team's skills and capacity, close the gaps and restructure it for a growing developer and publisher, deciding what we make in-house and what we outsource.

    Run a clear request process, from brief to delivery, with confident estimates of time, people and cost, and say no early when something isn't feasible.

    Deliver ad creatives, videos, store assets, key art, logos, trailers and in-game art support, within each game's art direction and licensor guidelines.

    Manage freelancers and outsourcing partners, own the team's budget and report on turnaround, cost and stakeholder satisfaction.

    Stay hands-on with paintovers, feedback and asset production, and keep improving pipelines and tools.

    An art background (2D, 3D, motion or video) with 6+ years in games including 2+ years managing artists or art production.

    Proven experience scoping, estimating, scheduling and budgeting art work, and comfortable working like a producer.

    Experience managing outsourcing studios and freelancers, from briefing to final delivery.

    Experience producing PC/Steam publishing assets (capsules, key art, trailers) and mobile UA creatives.

    A strong eye for quality and the ability to work within an existing art direction or style guide and give clear, actionable feedback.

    Industry observers note that solid understanding of art and video production pipelines, tools (e.g. Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects, Premiere Pro), file formats and delivery specs.

    Strong stakeholder management: you set clear expectations, communicate proactively and keep internal customers informed.

    Fluent written and spoken English.

    Excellent communication and collaboration within cross-functional and globally distributed teams.

    Experience building or restructuring a creative services, shared art or marketing art team.

    Experience working with licensed IP and licensor approval processes.

    Experience with game engines (e.g. Unity) and integrating in-game art assets.

    Proficiency in production tracking tools (e.g. Jira, ShotGrid, Notion or similar).

    Familiarity with AI-assisted art and video tools and how to use them responsibly in a production pipeline.

    Experience working with teams across different locations, cultures, and time zones.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're looking for a Platform Database Engineer to join our team to drive improvements to our internal databases.

    It has been revealed that the focus of this role is around owning stability and deployment of our internal databases. Supabase’s internal databases are the backbone of our service offerings. You will play a critical role in architecture and optimizations of the databases in partnership with the platform service teams, both strategically and tactically.

    In this role, your primary responsibilities will include:.

    Partnering closely with service teams to understand their workloads and growth, so our databases are sized, configured, and pooled to sustain current and future load.

    Performance tuning AWS RDS instances running postgres.

    Automation and Improvement to operations, including infrastructure as code and scripting.

    Schema and query optimizations across multiple services.

    Timely PostgreSQL major, minor, and extension upgrades.

    Engaging in proactive identification and resolution of production challenges in customer deployments.

    Spearheading the creation of best practices, tools, and tests to ensure enhanced stability and decreased deployment risks over time (minimal downtime, blue/green deployments, rollback intends).

    Incident response, including driving RCA and followups.

    This role demands the following pivotal qualities:.

    AWS RDS + PostgreSQL Expert: A profound understanding of PostgreSQL running on RDS and its associated tools (AWS Aurora experience also great!) . Familiarity with extensions, performance optimization, and best practices is essential. Experience with connection management (RDS proxy, Pgbouncer, Supervisor) is a huge plus.

    Infrastructure Obsessed: Proven expertise in infrastructure management, tooling, and optimization.

    Optimization Wizard. Engages across the full stack to identify bottlenecks and drives deep changes (architectural, code, process) that will completely resolve the challenge.

    Self-directed & Bias Towards Action: At Supabase, we value independence and proactive problem-solving, driving clarity in complex situations. We anticipate you to be a dynamic self-starter, thriving in asynchronous collaboration across diverse teams. Your knack for spotting areas of improvement and commitment to realizing those enhancements will be key. You'd rather ship a safe, incremental fix today than wait for the perfect redesign next quarter.

    Improve the utility and efficiency of our PostgreSQL offerings.

    Drive best practices across service teams; assisting with migrations and operations.

    Own tooling and solutions within the Supabase ecosystem.

    3+ years experience with PostgreSQL in AWS setting (RDS or Aurora).

    3+ years experience with infrastructure as code technology (terraform, pulumi).

    Computer Science Bachelors (or related field).

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    It has been revealed that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the firm. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Recent findings suggest that supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    Once a year, the entire firm gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.

    Christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh. This year, on-trend doesn’t have to mean brand-new—designers love decorating with heirloom pieces collected over time.

    However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.

    Recent findings suggest that this winter, our decor is taking a note from European culture—again. Swedish folk art is emerging as a hot winter trend in both holiday and home decor. Defined by bold red hues, tulip motifs, and S-scrolls, the style blends cozy-core with the heritage style craze.

    “European folk influences are so substantial right now,” says designer Johanna Lyle of Jo Lyle & Co. “Think Swedish Dala horses, quilt motifs, and decorative stitching. I think we will see those continue into holiday decor.”.

    According to recent reports, when it comes to her tree decor, interior designer Francesca Grace waves a hand at the carefully contrived, and she’s not alone. “My ornaments are collected from my travels, so the tree is really a collection of memories. I love unpacking them and remembering where each one came from. They don’t all match, and I wouldn’t want them to,” states Grace. “I let the ornaments lead. That mix feels much more personal to me, and it gives the tree something upcoming to say as the collection grows.” This year’s trends hinge on antiqued, inherited style, with one-off pieces that channel bold character and hardly ever come with a matching set.

    Interior designer Marie Flanigan likes to add a fresh twist to her seasonal decor with dried oranges and pops of cranberry red.

    “We've seen such a beautiful resurgence of dried citrus in holiday decorating over the past few years,” Flanigan explains. “And I think cranberries are ready for their moment to shine. Their rich red hue feels especially festive, and I love the idea of incorporating them into fresh greenery, draping them across a mantel, or pairing them with dried oranges for a more layered look.”.

    Recent findings suggest that if there’s one classic Christmas element Grace hopes makes a comeback, it's multicolored lights. Inherently nostalgic, these bold-hued bulbs were a ’90s staple.

    It has been revealed that “I’m ready for a little less restraint on the tree. Those reds, blues, greens, and yellows immediately bring back the feeling of Christmas as a child. They also pull together a collection of ornaments that might otherwise seem completely unrelated. White lights can be beautiful, but I want my Christmas tree to have some mischief,” says Grace.

    In a recent development, the classic red-and-green combination may take the title for the most iconic holiday palette, but this year, color trends are going complementary. While base colors stay warm and slightly rusted, patterned pieces are taking on cooler tones. This year, we’re also trading traditional plaid for Scottish tartan.

    “Warm crimsons, rich browns, tactile fabrics, and blue-green plaids make a beautiful holiday palette,” says Elizabeth Bennett, cofounder of the interior design firm Kobel + Co.

    According to recent reports, in a total rejection of mass-manufactured everything, handmade felt pieces are taking holiday homes by storm. The style has even coined a new holiday aesthetic: #Kitschmas, and, according to Lyle, it’s here to stay. “As AI continues to homogenize design, things made by humans will feel more special and important. Handmade and crafted items create stories around decor that feel meaningful and can be treasured year after year,” she states.

    It has been revealed that moody browns are steadily emerging as the fresh neutral as we inch closer to the new year, and lucky for our winter design schemes, the hue really is as versatile as it seems. Paired with powdery blues, bold crimsons, and even minty greens, chocolate brown grounds nearly any palette and matches every metallic hue.

    “I’m particularly drawn to chocolate brown as an unexpected foundation for holiday color palettes. It's incredibly rich and versatile. I love the idea of moving beyond traditional red and green and allowing the existing colors of a room to inform the holiday decor. You can create something incredibly festive through tonal layering, subtle metallic accents, and variations in material,” Flanigan explains.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

    Dreaming of Buying a Home Abroad? These 10 Countries Make It Shockingly Simple

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1220 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad.
    • Industry observers note that certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and Latest Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers.
    • Choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad. Moving internationally can often feel like a pipe dream, but with the right planning, it’s possible. However, lengthy visa processes, daunting language barriers, and a difficult-to-navigate legal system can make the dream feel more like a nightmare.

    Industry observers note that certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and Latest Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers. Others, like Thailand, Cuba, and Vietnam, don’t allow outsiders to own property at all. On the other end of the spectrum are countries actively trying to attract foreign buyers, offering enviable incentives like affordable home prices, a smoother customs process, and an easier-to-navigate work-visa approval process.

    Choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating. Ahead, we’re breaking down the ten best countries for Americans looking to buy property abroad. Whether you’re dreaming of relocating or searching for your perfect vacation home, these countries make buying as easy as possible and offer gorgeous landscapes too.

    If you’ve ever dreamed of living among medieval architecture and rolling mountain ranges, Georgia might be the key to unlocking your fantasy. A bridge between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, the transcontinental country borders Russia, Turkey, Armenia, and the Black Sea, offering both subtropical and high-altitude climates. Thankfully, the real estate landscape is much less complex, with few legal or bureaucratic hurdles for American buyers, no residency or visa required (for up to a year), and remarkably fast processing times. In fact, the only major restriction in the Georgia market is that foreigners cannot purchase or own agricultural land, a nod to the importance of the local, small-scale farming cultures peppered across the country’s regions.

    According to recent reports, uruguay’s buying process could not be more straightforward. South America’s second-smallest sovereign country requires no citizenship, visa, or prior approvals. Under Uruguayan law, foreign buyers are given the same rights as citizens and enjoy the benefits of free capital flow. Locals are just as, if not more, tourist-friendly. The country is known for its hospitality, laid-back café culture, and stunning coastal landscapes.

    In a recent development, instead of retiring to Florida, consider this balmy, beautiful Caribbean country—just a four-hour direct flight from the Newly introduced York area. Like everything else on the island, the real estate laws are relatively relaxed, making buying a house easy-breezy; and you can buy and own property without obtaining residency status or special permissions, as is the case in many other Caribbean islands. “Foreigners can own property outright in the Dominican Republic, with legal protections for foreign investors,” states Mauricio Umansky, CEO and founder of The Agency. One vital consideration is financing: You can certainly get a mortgage in the DR, but it may not be quite as cushy as what you can get in the U.S.—so pay cash if possible.

    Great news if you’ve been wanting a more provincial life: Americans face zero restrictions when buying homes in France. The open market allows for statesiders to buy houses, apartments, or plots of land in the city, countryside, and coastal towns in person or remotely without needing citizenship, residency, or even a local visa. However, a purchase does not grant residency, so if you’re hoping to make France your permanent home, you’ll want to apply for a separate long-stay visa and note the Schengen 90-out-of-180-day rule. While buying may be simple, the finances are anything but. Closing fees, including notary fees, typically add seven to ten percent to your purchase. Mortgage rates are also incredibly hard to secure for U.S.-based buyers, thanks to strict debt-to-income caps and FATCA compliance. To simplify the process, many buyers opt to put 20 percent to 40 percent down in cash.

    According to recent reports, perhaps the most American-friendly market, Panama boasts a large English-speaking market, virtually no restrictions on foreign property ownership, and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender in a vastly affordable market. The Central American nation also offers residency programs like the Friendly Nations Visa, clearing the way legally for residency by investment. In addition to an efficient legal system and reliable market, Panama boasts breathtaking beaches, lush rainforests, and exceptional wildlife.

    Sources indicate that if you’re hoping for a home in the coffee valleys of Colombia, you’ll need to hire a real estate lawyer before you start scouting for mountain chalets, coffee triangle treehouses, and rainforest retreats. The Caribbean country opts out of standardized agent licensing systems, making legal aid essential to verify title and freedom certificates. While citizenship isn’t required, you will need to secure a tourist visa and Colombian Tax ID to complete your purchase and register for property taxes.

    In a recent development, the buying process in Greece is lengthy, though it is streamlined, with a clear checklist for American buyers to find success in the market. Hiring a local lawyer or notary is a great first step after scouting properties. Not only are they familiar with title checks and contracts, but they can also navigate the intricacies that come with buying in designated border areas or near military zones, which require special clearance for non–EU buyers. While the most popular areas for American buyers, like Athens and Crete, don’t come with heavy legal intricacies, buying any property in Greece will mean securing a Greek Tax Number—a small price to pay for cities with such rich histories and breathtaking seaside views.

    The people in this popular Western European coastal country are famously friendly and inviting, and that extends to real estate. According to Samira Easton, a certified international property specialist with Premier Sotheby’s International Realty, Portugal offers a Golden Visa Program, which makes it simple to buy property and gain residency; clear real estate laws; and a well-established network of English-speaking real estate agents, lawyers, and notaries to help you during the process.

    According to recent reports, belize is home to one of the most vibrant, tourist-friendly cultures in Central America, mixing Mayan, Hispanic, Asian, and Creole cultures in its dense rainforests and rolling low plains. Buying here is as easy as it can get, as outright ownership applies to foreigners, and a British-inspired legal system abolishes language barriers and makes contracts easier to understand. Even more, there is no capital gains tax in Belize, and property taxes trend low. The country also boasts vibrant marine life and is home to the world’s second-largest barrier reef.

    Industry observers note that spain may have ended its investor visa program in 2025, but the real estate market is still remarkably easy for Americans to navigate. The country at the moment imposes no restrictions on foreign or nonresident property ownership, but there are a few things you’ll need to procure before you buy, like a Foreigner Identification Number, which is mandatory for taxes. Despite the minor hurdles, the market is booming both on the ground and online. “There are also numerous online resources and property portals available, so it’s easy to find listings and information,” Easton indicates. This is a boon for those who aren’t able to make the trip over to Europe to house shop in person.Note that buying property does not grant you residency or bypass the country’s 90-day Schengen limit. If you’re hoping to turn your Spanish holiday into your everyday, you’ll have to apply for a separate visa.

    #170867. 27 Charming Christmas Towns That Look Like a Real-Life Holiday Movie

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1266 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

    27 Charming Christmas Towns That Look Like a Real-Life Holiday Movie

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1266 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The holiday season is in full swing, with many halls and houses already decked to impress in garland and fairy lights.
    • These towns are more than just beautifully decorated—they’re truly immersive, offering experiences from Santa-themed bike rides to orchestrated light indicates and winter bar crawls.
    • In a recent development, this picturesque mountain town serves as the perfect holiday backdrop for more reasons than just the ever-present blanket of fluffy white snow.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The holiday season is in full swing, with many halls and houses already decked to impress in garland and fairy lights. But as you wrap gifts, prepare to host, and begin marathoning holiday movies, it can feel like the joyous season is coming to an end much too soon. We can't blame you if you're still wanting more from this merry time of year, and we've come up with a solution. There are plenty of beautiful Christmas towns across the country to fill your heart with peace, joy, and nostalgia—you just have to know where to look.

    These towns are more than just beautifully decorated—they’re truly immersive, offering experiences from Santa-themed bike rides to orchestrated light indicates and winter bar crawls. Below, we've rounded up the 27 most charming Christmas towns from all over the country, so no matter where you live, you'll be close enough to find a bit of extra cheer this year.

    Additional copy by Alyssa Khan.

    In a recent development, this picturesque mountain town serves as the perfect holiday backdrop for more reasons than just the ever-present blanket of fluffy white snow. Each year, the valley is transformed into a Christmas town with seasonal theatrical performances, Gunnison’s Night of Lights, a tree lighting ceremony, and even an ice sculpting event.

    It has been revealed that ever since the formation of this city on Christmas Eve in 1741, Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, has been rooted in the holiday spirit. From Christmas markets to historical tours to horse-drawn carriage rides, there's no doubt this town won't feel magical. And make sure to stop by the historic Sayre Mansion, pictured here, to check out their elegant holiday decor.

    It has been revealed that annapolis is known as one of the best cities during the holiday season thanks to its winter weather and historic downtown. If you're lucky enough to visit this Christmas town, make sure you spend time bargain shopping until midnight, checking out the spectacular light display in Sandy Point State Park, and viewing the Yacht Club Light Parade.

    Chicago is exceptionally beautiful during the Christmas time. From the seemingly endless strings of lights to the Christkindlmarket, which is free to enter and so charming, the Windy City has many offerings during the holiday season, making it one of the best Christmas towns to visit. Plus, you don't want to miss ice skating or any Christmas-themed museum exhibits.

    It has been revealed that if you want to do something Christmas-y almost every single day of December, then Newport, Rhode Island, might just be the place to go. To create the perfect coastal Christmas, this town offers a month-long celebration that's been going strong for 54 years. From holiday bike rides to Medieval festivals to winter afternoon teas, there's so much to do in this Christmas town.

    You'll feel as if you've traveled back to Charles Dickens's time when you walk through Franklin's historic Christmas festival. Characters from A Christmas Carol and Oliver Twist come to life throughout the weekend-long festivities. Roam the Victorian Village and try Victorian-era Christmas treats like sugar plums while listening to carolers.

    A classic ski town, Park City offers Christmas markets, festive decorations, and a Christmas Eve parade lit by torches—plus spectacular views of the mountains are around every corner.

    In the heart of Virginia horse country, you'll find one of the most festive Christmas towns. Cheer on the town's hunting hounds while sipping hard cider and wander the streets in search of vintage Christmas ornaments.

    During Kennebunkport's annual Christmas Prelude, the town puts on a very New England celebration: You can watch Santa Claus arrive by lobster boat, go on seashore holiday trolley rides, and enjoy wine tastings and lobster bakes. Not to mention, the town is covered in Christmas lights and garlands that make it the perfect festive photo backdrop.

    Recent findings suggest that for a dreamy and unique experience, head to Santa Fe. One of the most anticipated celebrations is the Canyon Road Farolito Walk, which is when thousands of farolitos—luminaries made of paper bags, sand, and tea candles—cast a glow on the gardens and old buildings that line the road. You also can get your white Christmas fix by visiting Ski Santa Fe.

    As one of the oldest towns in the country, Portsmouth is a charming Latest England destination that celebrates the holidays with a Vintage Christmas Celebration. Visit the historic village of Strawberry Banke or wander around the charming shopping districts in this historic Christmas town.

    It has been revealed that get a Hallmark movie feel while experiencing a taste of Denmark in California's Solvang village, located in Santa Ynez Valley wine country. The destination hosts Julefest, a month-long holiday celebration with live entertainment, a parade, and a night market.

    Recent findings suggest that koziar's Christmas Village in Bernville is one of the top attractions in Pennsylvania. With more than a million lights adorning buildings, barns, and the landscape—and a reflective lake that doubles the beauty—it's hard to beat the town's display.

    This Bavarian-style village is charming any time of year! December festivities include a display of Santa costumes from all around the world, a gingerbread house competition, carolers, and plenty of photo ops.

    It has been revealed that of course, Upcoming York City isn't a small Christmas town, but it is extra magical during the holidays. From the massive tree at Rockefeller Center to the various Christmas markets in the city parks with ice skating, shops, and more, you can't beat the Major Apple's holiday spirit.

    Nicknamed the Lighted Poinsettia Capital of Texas, this town brings major holiday spirit every year. Visit during December when the lighted trail in Comanche Trail Park is aglow all month long. Check out Hotel Settles for its elegant Art Deco lodging.

    In a recent development, during the holiday season, each home in Historic Williamsburg lights one candle, a tradition that dates back to the Revolutionary War era. The cobblestone streets and colonial holiday traditions such as caroling by torchlight make this destination a must, especially for history buffs.

    This Christmas town stays decked out year-round, so if you're craving holiday spirit in July, you'll still find candy-cane posts, boughs of holly, and a Santa Claus house with live reindeer!

    Christmas without the cold? We've got you covered! In addition to abundant sunshine and festive holiday decor, you'll also have plenty of history to explore in St. Augustine, America's oldest city.

    It has been revealed that want to take a ride on the Polar Express? Visit Durango during the holidays. The historic mining town offers a Polar Express–inspired trip that your kiddos will flip over.

Before becoming a home writer, Meghan worked in the fashion industry for two years, writing for Harper's Bazaar after graduating from Iowa State University with a bachelor's degree in apparel merchandising. When she's not interviewing interior designers about home trends, you can find Meghan reading a fictional thriller with her cat in her lap, planning themed parties, or strolling through flea markets searching for chunky candle holders and vintage bookends.

You might gain more attention at work, be up for a raise or promotion, or find that others are just gravitating toward you.     Industry observers note that here comes a wave of optimism thanks to Mercury entering Sagittarius on December 6. You’re more willing to say “yes” to opportunities that come your way and try a latest approach. You might be in a more social or adventurous mood—meeting new people, trying out new events, and pushing yourself outside of your comfort zone. You’re also feeling hopeful about some of your goals, finding new ways to pursue them and make progress on what excites you.

    A New Moon in Sagittarius gives you the faith necessary to chase after one of your dreams on December 8. This could show up as a job offer or a feeling of being in the right place at the right time. There is a serendipity quality to this new moon that helps you make aligned decisions about your future. It’s also possible a new friendship or alliance is formed, or you’re finally finding your place within a group or social circle that gives you purpose.

    Recent findings suggest that conversations are tough but help you address what you’ve ignored when Saturn stations direct in Aries on December 10. You might need to set a firm boundary or learn disappointing news. This can also bring contracts your way, but make sure you read the fine print and are being recognized for your worth, talent, and what you bring to the table before singing on the dotted line.

    Sources indicate that it’s easier than ever to share your feelings when Neptune stations direct in Aries on December 12. This energy is beautiful for journaling or creative writing. There’s some extra texture, charm, and warmth to your words. Healing conversations can also take place, bringing sensitive topics to the surface. This is also a great time to dust off your tarot deck and pick up a consistent spiritual practice or do some divination. Some interactions might be confusing, asking you to reflect on what is real vs. what is fantasy.

    According to recent reports, your relationships are undergoing seismic changes when Jupiter stations retrograde in Leo, also on December 12. This can feel like an all-or-nothing moment, causing larger ripple effects in your closest connections. You could have a conversation or interaction with someone that tests the foundation of your relationship, prompting more reflection before you make any major decisions. There could also be a development regarding a contract or client relationship—a turning point that will take some time to unpack before you decide what comes next or how you want to react.

    In a recent development, the Sun enters Capricorn and the Winter Solstice takes place on December 21, encouraging you to spend some time alone. You might be socially drained and this isn’t the time to give into FOMO. Spending time alone and even honing a spiritual practice—whether that’s an evening walk, nightly meditations, or something your Ancestors practiced—will bring you the grounding, clarity, and guidance that you seek.

    A Full Moon in Cancer on December 23 helps you change up your lifestyle. If there are certain habits and patterns that have kept you repeating the same old cycles and living in an eternal groundhog day, this is your chance to make a change. You might also deal with a reality check regarding your own wellbeing, recognizing you have to stop sacrificing your body, mind, and spirit’s needs to keep other people happy. Setting boundaries and finding a more consistent routine for self-care can be just what you need.

    The month wraps up with you relying more on your intuition once Mercury enters Capricorn on December 25. Your connection to the other Realms is evident, and you’re trusting your own instincts more and more. You might also feel more exhausted and worn down. This energy can show up when you’re struggling with insomnia, overextending yourself, or needing to be accountable for your own behaviors. This can help you close out cycles and situations in your life that have run its course by confronting the programming that’s running in the background of your subconscious. It’s time for an upgrade!

    Sources indicate that the Sun enters Capricorn on December 21, marking the Winter Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere and the longest night of the year. This is not the time to overdo it or overextend yourself. It’s time to prune people, patterns, and situations from your life that extinguish your drive and essence instead of replenishing them. A Full Moon in Cancer on December 23, highlights your relationship with the past, primary caregivers, and security. There’s no need to sugarcoat to keep others comfortable, your time is limited and you’ve got things to do!     Before & After: This Couple Planned to Flip a 62-Year-Old Fixer-Upper, Then Made It Their Home Instead

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything.
    • Built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades.
    • Recent findings suggest that the decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything. In 2021, she and her now-husband, Will, purchased a nearly 5,000-square-foot home in Jackson, Mississippi’s Eastover neighborhood, with plans to renovate the property and flip it for a profit. By 2022, they were engaged in the unfinished kitchen. Four years later, they’re still there, now with a baby daughter and a house that looks very little like the one they originally intended to sell.

    Built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades. The rooms were compartmentalized, the finishes were dated, and the quirky floor plan presented a few head-scratching challenges, like a second-floor dining room entirely removed from the kitchen below. But Thompson, who introduced her design business in 2020, saw something worth holding onto. “I promptly fell in love with the bones of the home, the lot the home is positioned on, and of course the neighborhood and the street itself,” she recalls.

    Recent findings suggest that the decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach. Rather than gutting the house and putting in finishes they knew would grab buyers in a post-COVID market, the couple worked within the home’s existing footprint, opening up walls to encourage better circulation while preserving the individuality of each room. The kitchen, once closed off at either end, now connects to a light-filled breakfast nook and an inviting keeping room, where damaged parquet floors and dated ceiling beams gave way to white oak underfoot and softly textured plaster overhead.

    Nearby, a former study became an inky, book-lined library, complete with an expanded bar. Even the upstairs dining room survived, despite its logistical inconveniences. “We decided to keep it because of the way it flows when we entertain and host showers or parties,” Thompson claims. “I think a home that tells a story, like a nod to the past or an interesting quirk, only makes the home more intriguing.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the renovation unfolded after hours, with Will building cabinetry and tackling electrical work late into the night. Some spaces were even renovated twice: first, with resale in mind, then with the more personal considerations of permanence. The home became a testing ground for Thompson’s design practice, but it also serves as something of a family scrapbook. “We grew together as individuals, as a couple, as business owners, and as creatives,” she states. “The home feels like us.”.

    FAST FACTSDesigner: Claire Thompson DesignLocation: Jackson, MississippiThe Space: A five-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bathroom home across 5,000 square feet.

    The kitchen layout didn’t change too much, but Thompson was able to completely upgrade its feel and functionality by opening up both ends—one to the breakfast nook, one to the keeping room—and adding a center island.

    “I really did not want upper cabinets in the kitchen, so we were very thoughtful in the functionality of the cabinetry,” she adds. “My husband loves to remind me that he built me 42 drawers for the kitchen. We have ample storage, while still making it aesthetically the way I envisioned.”.

    Industry observers note that now open to the kitchen, the breakfast nook acts as a natural overflow spot where the family eats most of their meals, casual dinners included. Removing the ceiling beams allowed Thompson to capture the feel of taller ceilings; while she wanted to keep the brick floors, opening up the walls meant she had to opt for new white oak for continuity.

    “We call this the keeping room since we opened it up to the kitchen,” explains Thompson. “This is the room we really live in day to day; it’s a laid-back and comfortable space.”.

    It has been revealed that the pair started by plastering just the fireplace, but then decided to extend the treatment throughout the rest of the room—it’s since become a signature finish for Thompson’s firm. “We now use this technique in almost every project,” she adds.

    Industry observers note that previously a study, the library was born of equal parts design instincts and necessity. “My husband has so many books that we decided to wrap the room with bookshelves,” explains Thompson, who also reworked a hallway to add a bar and powder bathroom. The whole space is drenched in a Roman clay finish (Black Star by Portola Paints), creating an enveloping retreat that has become a go-to for family movie nights.

    Recent findings suggest that also known as the family’s “Christmas tree room,” the formal living room is a soothing symphony of neutral hues and nubby textures. “The coffee table is one of my favorite purchases of all time,” Thompson adds. “I bought it to sell to a client but decided I couldn’t part with it! I also love to have my grandmother’s antique stool in here—it always makes me think of her and brings me joy.”.

    Perfectly balanced between sweet and sophisticated, 12-week-old daughter Margot’s bedroom was an opportunity for Thompson to lean into all things childhood magic. “She may never leave the bassinet in our primary bedroom, but she does have a cute room waiting for her if that ever happens!” she adds.

    It has been revealed that connected to the nursery through a Jack-and-Jill bathroom, this guest space could eventually become a bedroom for a second child. For now, though, it’s a comfortable spot for visiting guests, and a favorite hideout of Thompson’s “first baby,” pup Lemmon.

    Recent findings suggest that claire Thompson is the owner of Claire Thompson Design, a full-service firm specializing in designing, renovating, and furnishing beautiful, timeless homes. She works closely with clients to ensure their unique personalities and desires are perfectly captured by the design and that all their wishes and needs are met.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that everyone plays video games, but not everybody is a gamer. If the person you are shopping for lives and breathes games reviews, spends their days on Discord and their nights streaming, and took days off work to play Grand Theft Auto VI, you have a real gamer on your hands. They are dedicated to their fandom, so they deserve someone who is dedicated to getting them a good gift. Consider this guide your cheat code.

    It doesn’t matter who you are buying for; we always start with the same ground rules around here. A good gift should be something unexpected but also something that, once they start using it, they can’t live without. Many of us would love a new headset or chair and we don’t even realize it. A fancy new controller never hurt, but if you want to go even deeper, we’ve done the digging for you. The best piece of advice we have for buying gifts for gamers? Ask them what they like, where they play, the basics. This will help you get a picture of which gifts are appropriate and which are going to suck the air out of the room.

    Below is our curated list of the gifts all gamers are sure to appreciate. These are the 32 best gifts for gamers that won’t embarrass them.

    It has been revealed that if sales numbers indicate anything, they likely already have purchased a copy. If they didn’t, GTA VI is the only gift worth giving a gamer this holiday. Go ahead, make their year.

    Industry observers note that yeah, it’s a big purchase—maybe split it with some other loved ones—but there is no better gaming chair on the market. This is one that will improve the overall look of their home. You can’t say that about many gaming chairs.

    Let them put their feet up during their next Saturday-night raid session and they will thank you in the morning.

    If they need somewhere to put the headset they already have, none look as good as this one that combines natural walnut wood and gamers’ beloved LEDs.

    Sometimes you’re trying to fill out a gift guide and stumble upon a gift that is perfect for you (the writer). This Shark Tank wonder allows gamers to easily enjoy messy snacks like Doritos, Cheetos—anything with dust, really. See also: candy and sticky sweets. If they like to snack during the cutscenes, this is the gag gift to get ’em.

    Industry observers note that it’s the collaboration of the decade, the biggest team-up since Avengers: Endgame. Nintendo and Lego have come together to make the best gift for nostalgic gamers who miss the halcyon days of the Game Boy. It’s also the coolest Lego set in years. Win-win.

    In a recent development, if your cousin plays Street Fighter 6 obsessively, get them this classy fight stick to give ’em a competitive edge. This one is compatible with any PC setup as well as with Nintendo Switch.

    If you want a little hit of nostalgia, these small emulation machines from Miyoo let you play hundreds of 8-, 16-, and 32-bit-era games from SNES to GBA.

    This is going to be the most sought-after item for gamers this holiday season. Get ahead of the curve and buy one now before they become tough to get your hands on.

    If they already have a Switch 2 (and you’ll know, because you won’t have seen or heard from them since last June), this is the best accessory you can get for them. It’s a travel case with room for a dozen game carts, and best of all it charges your console on the go. No more showing up to Pokémon trading night out of juice.

    A more sophisticated alternative to those RGB string lights they already have.

    Back in 2023, these earned an Esquire Gaming Award, and we’re still rocking them, even as we’ve seen the industry follow suit. This is still one of the best headsets you can get for your dearest gamer who switches between console and PC.

    Essentially, it connects via a Bluetooth adapter, but it can connect to multiple devices at a time. That means switching from Xbox to PlayStation to PC audio requires only the flip of a switch. It happens instantly, like changing the channel. If they are a multiplatform gamer, it’s one of the coolest gifts you can get.

    If the Series X (or S) is your chosen console—and you don’t actually own any games and just pay for Game Pass—this is the headset you need. SteelSeries makes more advanced headsets with bigger dongles, but we love the Nova 7 series for its simplicity and ease of use. Sound and mic quality are top-notch as well.

    If they like to lean back and play on their handheld, I bet you didn’t know you could get them something this perfect. Pick the console grip for their device of choice (Steam Deck, Nintendo Switch, ROG Ally X, and PlayStation Portal are all options) and they will never game uncomfortably again.

    Everything we’ve ever said about the Quest 3 is true about the lighter, cheaper, and more mixed-reality-focused Quest 3S. In our opinion, the all-in-one VR headset is still the absolute best way to get into virtual reality. There are games, fitness apps, and all the immersive demos you need in order to stay entertained for months. And you can finally get one of these for a gift-appropriate price.

    Recovery is essential to any athlete. And yes, we’ll give esports professionals the title of athlete (for this purpose at least). These Therabody goggles will massage away any screen fatigue or headache from a too-long gaming session.

    If you know someone who wants to get into streaming, this most affordable model of the Elgato Stream Deck is a great place to start. It will help them bring up the programs and links they need at the touch of a button (or eight).

    A fun little DIY screen break for the kid obsessed with Minecraft (Jack Black not included).

    For those cozy Sunday mornings when they are snuggling up on the couch with a hot cup of coffee and their PS5. You can even get them one that matches the color of their console (probably white).

    What’s cooler than our fanciest gaming-headset rec? This wearable speaker from Panasonic, designed to give gamers an even more immersive audio experience without total isolation, so your spouse won’t lose their mind.

    Tech Report: 50 Percent of People In Relationships Would Take a Trip Together to Solve Their Problems

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
    • Sources indicate that A “baecation” often entails a romantic getaway, passionate activities, and a lot of vacation sex.
    • It has been revealed that according to Booking.com’s 2027 Travel Predictions, 58 percent of U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

    Sources indicate that A “baecation” often entails a romantic getaway, passionate activities, and a lot of vacation sex. But what if traveling with your significant other meant a lot of difficult conversations, a heated back-and-forth, and working to fix your relationship. I know: this sounds nothing like the dreamy R&R you pictured—but for some couples, it’s exactly what they planned for.

    It has been revealed that according to Booking.com’s 2027 Travel Predictions, 58 percent of U.S. travelers mentioned they would consider taking a trip to resolve conflicts or arguments.

    Sources indicate that now, traveling itself already can cause real strain and arguments on relationships on its own. In the same data set, more than one-third of respondents mentioned they found out they were incompatible with their companion after a trip. Nearly three in 10 people have considered ending a relationship or friendship over a trip, while more than one in five have actually cut a vacation short because of a bad travel companion.

    It has been revealed that but if you’re already having relationship issues with your partner, is a trip a good idea? People still seem to think so. About 81 percent noted that taking part in at least one vacation activity with another person helps them have honest or difficult conversations.

    So should you be planning a trip the next time you and your partner start arguing?

    A change of scenery might be exactly what you and your partner need to see eye-to-eye again.

    “Getting away from work, chores, kids, in-laws, or house and childcare stuff can lower defenses,” couples therapist Justena Kavanagh tells Cosmopolitan.

    She explains that when you’re home, you’re essentially having every argument on the same “battleground.”.

    It has been revealed that “Somewhere latest often brings back the honeymoon period, when you could really see each other without life’s stresses in the way,” she states. And if both you and your partner have busy lives and packed schedules, a vacation may really be the only time you can focus on the problems in your relationship without distraction.

    Plus, vacations encourage you to relax—which can go a long when in an argument. “When we’re rested, we’re more regulated, and when we’re regulated, we can listen instead of defending,” Kavanagh indicates.

    In a recent development, she explains that it’s important to establish why exactly you’re going on the vacation in the first place. Are you getting away to talk about an issue? Or simple to get away from it and reconnect? Agreeing on the purpose for the trip before you start packing your bikini will help you and your partner get on the same page—so you don’t end up just arguing more later.

    “Trips suit conversations about connection, like feeling distant, intimacy, or where the relationship is going,” she indicates. Other things like finances or in-law conflicts may need a follow-up at home.

    Sources indicate that if you decide that you’re going to talk your challenges out, remember that you are still on vacation. That doesn’t mean everything has to be wonderful, of course. But Kavanagh encourages couples to treat the trip like a summit. This means talking early in the day (after a good night’s rest) and working on things while taking breaks.

    The trip should essentially be your opportunity to discuss what’s currently happening in the relationship, where you want the relationship to go, and how to shift priorities to get there.

    Sure, a beautiful view and hotel sex will definitely lighten the mood and probably even make you more agreeable—but it isn’t a magical bandaid for your relationship problems.

    “If couples don’t have relational skills at home, they won’t miraculously have them on vacation,” Kavanagh warns.

    So if you’re going to go on a vacation to work on things with your partner, you’re going to want to put a plan into place. The best method? Talking about the pattern behind the argument, rather than hyperfocusing on the latest incident.

    And even if you do come to a resolution on vacation, make sure you’re setting a plan in place for the positive energy to flow into your everyday lives.

    “Be realistic about home, where you’re more stressed and old patterns return fast,” Kavanagh says. “Strategy follow-up support, a regular check-in, and what you’ll do when things go off track, because they will.”.

    Okay, so not all of us can afford to book a flight every time we get into an argument with our partner—but you don’t have to. Out of all the activities that people do on vacation, respondents noted that it was mostly hikes or walking that was the most effective at getting them to open up and have the difficult conversations.

    Lucky for you, taking a hike is totally free—and can do wonders for whatever issue you may be facing with your partner.

    Kavanagh explains that walking and hiking take pressure off of an argument.

    It has been revealed that “Face to face can feel like a confrontation; side by side, you’re facing the same direction and don’t have to hold eye contact in the hardest moments,” she explains. This is something we see in psychotherapy: think about someone lying on a couch, looking at the ceiling. This helps physiologically and emotionally. Plus the actual physical activity helps, too.

    “Walking also discharges stress and is a natural form of bilateral stimulation, the left-right rhythm used in therapies like EMDR,” she says.

    In a recent development, when your partner is irritating you, it’s likely that the last thing you want to do is travel with them. But if you’re determined to move past whatever may be causing a rift, that might be exactly what you need.

    Honeymoons and other happy occasions shouldn’t be the only time we travel with our partners with the purpose of growing closer, reconnecting, and strengthening the relationship. Sometimes, even in hardship, a little getaway could be the jumpstart your relationship needs to get back on track. Just remember that after the vacation ends, you do have to go back to reality.

    “The good feelings are real, but the test is whether they last back home, where life is harder,” Kavanagh states.

    Recent findings suggest that I’m still not over this preppy schoolboy-inspired look from 2023, which centers around a polo shirtdress and knee-high maple-hued boots.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that we all know design is reflective. Whether it’s in our personal style, architectural splendor, or cultural ties, great design mirrors the world around us. Now, it’s time for it to mirror itself.

    Once dismissed as a tacky, ’70s-era trend (not unlike wood paneling), mirrored surfaces are making a comeback. But don’t worry—today’s mirror craze moves past the floor-to-ceiling panels of the past, opting instead for accents that add light, depth, and dimension.

    According to recent reports, “I love mirrored surfaces in interiors because they can be so transformative & work in all styles. They can add glitz and glamour, especially when you add beveled details,” says Bridget Tiek of TIEK BYDAY. “I love to see mirrors as a backbar, behind shelves, on doors, ceilings and on walls. Basically everywhere!”.

    Bolder than traditional ready-to-hang mirrors, mirrored surfaces are often hard to place tastefully. Here’s how designers have brought the striking detail into interiors.

    According to recent reports, queer Eye for the Straight Guy star Carson Kressley’s Murray Hill apartment is full of personality, and his sunken living room has several glittering surfaces. The designer embraces mirrored shine as a bold accent, as seen in this disco-ball-tiled end table.

    Use It for a Bold Bar Backsplash.

    Designer Alexander D. Wilson brought a mirrored backsplash into this Upper East Side apartment to elevate the elegant yet fun palette while creating the illusion of a larger space. NYC apartments often feel like a shoebox. With this classic design trick, they don’t have to look like it.

    Sources indicate that interior designer Sarah Vaile brought Manhattan to the Windy City in this punchy coastal home. After coating the walls in Farrow & Ball’s Borrowed Light for a classic Nancy Meyers-esque aesthetic, she framed a nearly ceiling-high mirror in crisp white molding, transforming the panel into a bold decorative piece that amplifies space and cosmopolitan chic.

    Incorporate as a Tasteful Touch.

    Bold enough to make a fierce statement in even the smallest piece, interior designer Amy Courtney brought industrial flair to her New York City home with a silvery domed lamp to complement the bold hues of her living room’s palette.

    While the glassy, expansive nature of mirrored panels certainly has its charms, if you’re hoping to bring both glossy and textured flair to your design, mirrored tiles are the perfect solution. Designer Shannon Ggem used mirrored tiles in this moody bar design to bring more light to the room without sacrificing the deep-hued palette.

    Recent findings suggest that while most rely on millwork to bring style to the walls, designer Michelle Prentice opted for mirror panels on the closet doors of this South Carolina bedroom. Not only do they add depth to the design, but they bring a boutique feel while adding to the visual palette and playing off the centered vanity mirror to unify the wall treatments.

    Sources indicate that as stainless steel fades from an industry standard to a passing fad, designers are getting creative when it comes to finding chic alternatives. In this monochrome green butler’s pantry, designer Bridget Tiek brought in a glassy paneled door to elevate the appliance design, taking the invisible kitchen trend to new heights.
