    Latest Update: Claude Intros Sonnet 5.5 with Model-Switching Cybersecurity Safeguards

    📅 08 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that anthropic's newly introduced Claude release, Sonnet 5.5, brings cybersecurity safeguards that can change which model handles a request during a Claude conversation.
    • According to Anthropic's explanation of model switching, automatic fallback is enabled by default in Claude.
    • In a recent development, the company identifies penetration testing and exploit generation among activities that may trigger cybersecurity fallbacks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that anthropic's newly introduced Claude release, Sonnet 5.5, brings cybersecurity safeguards that can change which model handles a request during a Claude conversation. Higher-risk tasks can fall back to Sonnet 5.

    According to Anthropic's explanation of model switching, automatic fallback is enabled by default in Claude. Users receive a notice, and the answer is labeled with the model that provided it. The chat then stays on Sonnet 5 unless the user changes the selection.

    In a recent development, the company identifies penetration testing and exploit generation among activities that may trigger cybersecurity fallbacks. Source-code vulnerability scanning remains supported. Biology and reasoning-extraction safeguards can block requests outright, rather than route them elsewhere.

    In a recent development, the distinction matters operationally. A block stops the request; a fallback allows an attempt to continue with a different model. Neither outcome should be treated as interchangeable with completion by the model the user originally chose.

    In a recent development, anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and can reduce cost per task by up to 30%, based on its testing. Token prices remain unchanged.

    Industry observers note that those claims describe performance under the manufacturer's test conditions. An organization evaluating the service also needs to examine what happens when its own assignments encounter safeguards.

    It has been revealed that an internal pilot could record how often work is interrupted, whether fallback answers are usable, and when users need help. Such measurements would give buyers a more relevant basis for deployment than assuming every task receives the advertised model's capabilities.

    Anthropic has revealed aims to expand its Cyber Verification Program with tiered access for Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, and Mythos models. Its current program guidance explicitly excludes the two upcoming 5.5 models and claims the expansion is forthcoming.

    Organizations should distinguish those planned arrangements from access available today.

    According to recent reports, the broader enterprise issue is accountability. When an AI service changes models during an assignment, someone still needs to determine whether the resulting work is suitable. A visible handoff helps, but organizations must decide how employees should respond to it.

    For more information on Sonnet 5.5, go to the Anthropic site.

    16 Festive Holiday Date Ideas for the Most Wonderful Time of Year

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Iam here to debunk a common dating myth: Despite what all the relationship gurus might suggest, dating doesn’t have to be confined to the summer.
    • According to recent reports, sure, the urge to snuggle up with your coziest blanket and binge your favorite rom-coms is nagging you and your person—I get it.
    • Volunteering as a date night is a great way to see someone’s generous side.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Iam here to debunk a common dating myth: Despite what all the relationship gurus might suggest, dating doesn’t have to be confined to the summer. In fact, some of the best, most romantic dates can happen during the late fall and dead of winter. After all, every street and tree is covered in twinkling lights and the cold weather gives you an excuse (not that you need one) to cozy up next to your crush. Add the festivities of the holiday season on top of all of that and you literally have the makings of a dream date.

    According to recent reports, sure, the urge to snuggle up with your coziest blanket and binge your favorite rom-coms is nagging you and your person—I get it. But this holiday season is the time to make your Hallmark movie dreams a reality! Whether you’re looking for an option for a third date with someone you just started seeing or trying to keep things fresh and fun in your long-term relationship, there’s something on this list for you.

    Volunteering as a date night is a great way to see someone’s generous side. Find a local donation center, soup kitchen, or a cause that means a lot to you. You’ll be able to tell a lot about your date by their reaction to this idea and how they carry themselves throughout the volunteering.

    Sources indicate that this one will really test your teamwork. You can either grab a premade kit or go old-school and use a pint-sized milk carton and graham crackers as your base. Some of the premade are pretty simple, while others can be a bit more intricate. Either way, both will force you and your date to work together and problem solve. This will be a good way for those red flags or green flags to show themselves.

    Because it’s time you get in on the whole matching pajamas and Santa hats. If you don’t want to put out money for a photographer, set up your phone’s camera with a timer and tripod—the photos can look just as amazing!

    Recent findings suggest that elevate your hot chocolate game with fun flavors, like salted caramel, dark chocolate, or peppermint. You can buy premade variety packs or really chef it up with making your own. Whatever you choose, just be sure not to skim on the toppings. Grab marshmallows of all sizes, candy canes, whipped cream (I personally love the boozy vodka-infused peppermint one from Whipshots), and whatever else sounds enticing. You will be chocolate wasted and it will be fantastic.

    Sources indicate that karaoke isn’t about who sounds the best but who has the best energy. Belt out your favorite holiday jams, from the classics to upcoming renditions of the season’s most popular songs. It’s truly a perfect way to bond and see if your date can match your vibe.

    This option is such a fun way to spend time together. Whether this is an early date with someone you recently started seeing or an activity you and your longtime love do, it’s great for talking, asking questions, and having fun. If you’re a part of the first group, this can be an opportunity to make a candle for each other—then you could exchange them as a low-stakes holiday gift (because getting a present for your situationship is always tricky).

    It has been revealed that if you or your date are people who appreciate a good aesthetic, finding a local light show could be the perfect night out. The low lighting and colorful moments can help you draw closer to your person, whether it’s in the car riding through or walking. Light shows leave room for more intimate conversations to take place, too, if you want that.

    Industry observers note that the best way to spread holiday cheer is by supporting local businesses. From small batch food to unique clothes and accessories, it’s where you and your partner can shop for each other or grab gifts for loved ones. Oftentimes, these events also have other activities available nearby, like ice skating or photo moments, making for the perfect two-in-one date.

    Bring out the creative energy with a cutesy arts and crafts moment. Grab a few blank ornaments, brushes and bottles of paint, stickers, fabric, and whatever else strikes your fancy. Set it all up on a flat surface (like a dining table or floor), throw in a few Christmas songs and snacks, and you’ve got the makings of a simple and fun at-home holiday date night.

    Sources indicate that speaking of not making date night complicated, a simple stroll through your neighborhood (or perhaps one that’s more festive than yours) can still be made special. Make some boozy hot chocolates or hotty toddies, strap in to all your cold-weather gear, and sidewalk hike through your community. Bonus points for lots of hand holding, hugging, kissing and gossiping about the neighbors inflatable holiday characters in their front yard.

    “Do you want to build a snowman?” Anna from Frozen isn’t the only one who can enjoy the feeling of holiday magic. Similar to ornament decorating and gingerbread house making, building a snowman is the ultimate nostalgia cheat code. While he might not come to life like Olaf, dressing him up with the cutest scarf and hat will still be just as worthwhile.

    Industry observers note that the intentionality behind handwritten notes will forever show true thoughtfulness. This idea allows the two of you to really get creative with one another and reflect on who in your lives you want to wish a happy holiday season. Whether you’re sending our joint cards or individual ones, let your heartfelt emotions shine through.

    Can you technically do this any time of the year? Yes. But walk with me: What makes sporting events special for the holiday season is the amount of on-the-ground activations and curated experiences that teams provide fans. I’m talking seasonal menus galore, holiday-themed lounges, and activations where you can put your partner’s competitive skills to the test. It’s almost like a bunch of dates in one!

    Warm up from the brisk cool air outside by attending a wine tasting at your local winery or private holiday-themed events. Wines with notes of cocoa, hints of spice, and earthiness are especially great to lean into for rich flavor. They also pair well with heavier meals that people typically enjoy during the winter months.

    Love the snow but hate the cold? Search for the nearest igloo dining restaurant near you for a winter lunch or dinner. Usually, the igloos are kind of snug (but not in an uncomfortable way), giving you at-home levels of cozy with a space heater or bonfire. They’re also super festive with the decor, so you and your date will feel all the holiday cheer.

    Tom Hardy's 5 Most Stylish Characters, Ranked

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy.
    • That’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own.
    • So, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy. He’s been a forger, a fixer, a getaway driver, a rogue spy, and, in one of his more ambitious films, both halves of the most notorious twins in British crime (not that there’s much competition). Most of them are walking red flags, sure, but they’re red flags in great clothes.

    That’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own. Put him in a Western shirt or three-piece and he’ll look equally at home in both (and you’ll want to steal the look, either way).

    So, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now. Consider it your new watch list—just ignore the red flags.

    Everyone remembers the spinning top and Joseph Gordon-Levitt’s three-piece, but the best-dressed man in Inception is the one who usually gets overlooked: Tom Hardy’s Eames. Costume designer Jeffrey Kurland imagined him as an expat from a Graham Greene novel, and every piece was made from scratch (even though half of it looks straight off a Dries Van Noten runway). Think batik-print shirts, collars spread over relaxed blazers, sharp trousers, and a wallet chain—basically clothes for a guy who spends too long sitting in the sun and definitely doesn’t wear SPF. Then there’s the watch: a gold tank-style antique Kurland picked up from the prop master’s collection—and he’s since forgotten the brand. Reddit’s watch sleuths are still on the case, 16 years and counting.

    Legend gave its costume department a very vital task: how do you tell Tom Hardy apart from Tom Hardy? Lead designer Caroline Harris and Soho tailor Chris Kerr solved it with buttons: Reggie, the charmer, wears single-breasted suits that feel safe and easy to trust. Ronnie, meanwhile, is the volatile one who gets three-piece double-breasted silhouettes with extra padding to make him look macho. On both sides, though, everything’s cut from vintage fabrics for a lived-in look straight from the hanger. Sixty years on, you could walk into any hotel bar dressed as either and nobody would bat an eye. Until you start talking business, that is.

    Sources indicate that inspired by the real-world Cold War scandals that rocked British Intelligence, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy follows the hunt for a Russian mole inside MI6 in 1973. So, as you might expect, it’s lots of men doing stuff in gray suits. Not Hardy’s Ricki Tarr, though. He’s the only agent with any personality, wardrobe-wise, all thanks to costume designer Jacqueline Durran. Her thinking? Steve McQueen on a mission: a shearling coat in Istanbul, a Baracuta Harrington in Paris, and not a standard suit in sight. The kind of menswear every guy on your FYP is wearing today—Hardy was just 15 years early.

    In MobLand, Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren head up the Harrigans, an Irish crime family at war on several fronts—and no one knows it better than Hardy. He plays Harry Da Souza, the guy they call when things go wrong, which seems to happen fairly often. Costume designer Rebecca Hale gave him a wardrobe for the job: a battered wax jacket when he’s taking care of the Cotswolds estate, say, or a substantial overcoat when he’s doing business in the city. There’s one exception to the low-key menswear staples, though: his watch. In season one, he wore a solid gold Rolex GMT-Master II, which is reportedly the most valuable watch in the show. Pretty good for the hired help.

    MobLand isn’t Hardy’s first Guy Ritchie gangster part. In RocknRolla, he’s Handsome Bob, the Wild Bunch’s getaway driver. And while everyone else looks like they’d had someone ‘”taken care of” before lunch, Hardy’s low-key menswear staples make him look more like the boy next door. A faded denim shirt. A classic bomber with jeans. A blue checked Western shirt, open just far enough. All simple pieces that let his charm do its thing, which it does when he sweet-talks a lawyer into revealing who’s been grassing to the police. Four years earlier, he played Clarkie in Layer Cake, another member of a London crime crew but one with a very different wardrobe: slicked hair, blazers, open shirts, brandy, and cigars. Similar JD, just with a very different wardrobe.

    Convergence of AI, Quantum Risks Is Impacting Cybersecurity

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent research from Thales highlights how AI adoption and emerging quantum computing threats are putting pressure on existing security measures.
    • The research, conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global, examines both the risks and potential benefits of the technologies.
    • Cloud-based storage, cloud-delivered applications, and cloud management infrastructure were the three most frequently cited asset types targeted by attackers, at 35%, 34%, and 32%, respectively.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent research from Thales highlights how AI adoption and emerging quantum computing threats are putting pressure on existing security measures. The 2026 Thales Data Threat Report: Quantum & AI Trends, based on responses from 3,120 security and IT management professionals across 20 countries, found that 98% are considering how the two technologies affect each other. Thirty percent reported a significant increase in security budgets specifically for AI.

    The research, conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global, examines both the risks and potential benefits of the technologies. Fifty-seven percent believe quantum computing will enhance machine learning, while 54% expect it to enable advanced simulations of complex systems. The security findings span data governance, cloud infrastructure, and preparations for quantum-resistant encryption.

    Cloud-based storage, cloud-delivered applications, and cloud management infrastructure were the three most frequently cited asset types targeted by attackers, at 35%, 34%, and 32%, respectively. The report connects that exposure to the large datasets required for AI training and the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

    In a recent development, organizations are also looking to cloud providers for protection: 67% reported investing in their cloud provider's AI-specific security tools, compared with 63% using an established security provider. Respondents could identify multiple sources of protection, including startups, large language model providers, and internally developed controls.

    Industry observers note that encryption coverage remains incomplete. Only 7% of organizations reported encrypting more than 80% of their sensitive cloud data, while 29% reported encrypting more than 60%. The report's chart puts the average share encrypted at 47% in 2026, down from 51% in 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that the findings extend concerns raised in coverage of Thales' 2025 cloud security research, when AI security already ranked second to cloud security in spending priorities and 52% of respondents reported that AI security spending was displacing existing security budgets. The latest report again places AI security second, while its historical comparison shows average sensitive cloud data encryption coverage falling from 51% in 2025 to 47% in 2026.

    AI security was the second-highest prioritized security spending category overall, behind cloud security. But protecting data ranked much lower among the measures organizations use to judge AI projects: Reducing or managing risks of data loss or noncompliance placed sixth among seven success criteria, at 35%.

    According to recent reports, improving customer experience led those measures at 68%, followed by reducing employee toil through greater task automation at 63%. Meanwhile, poor data quality or initial data governance was the leading inhibitor to AI adoption, cited by 65%; security risks from exposed data followed at 61%. Another 51% cited AI initiatives moving too quickly to be properly secured.

    A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

    Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.

    Class CrunchLabs, the suite of free curriculum resources from NASA engineer turned YouTube science communicator Mark Rober, has released its first two courses on YouTube.

    Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network concerns can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a recent study from ControlUp.

    #170811. Flashpoint Receives Patent for Ransomware Risk Model, Tying Vulnerabilites to Likelihood of Attack

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (782 w)

    Flashpoint Receives Patent for Ransomware Risk Model, Tying Vulnerabilites to Likelihood of Attack

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (782 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that cybersecurity manufacturer Flashpoint unveiled it has received U.S.
    • The patent comes at a time when security teams are confronting a growing vulnerability problem: Flashpoint's Global Threat Intelligence Report: 2026 Midyear Edition tracked 21,667 vulnerability disclosures during the first half of 2026, an 8% increase.
    • Of those, 4,015, or around 19 percent, already had public or functional exploit code.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that cybersecurity manufacturer Flashpoint unveiled it has received U.S. Patent No. 12,705,360 for its Ransomware Risk model, a methodology designed to help security teams determine which newly disclosed vulnerabilities more closely resemble those historically used in ransomware attacks.

    The patent comes at a time when security teams are confronting a growing vulnerability problem: Flashpoint's Global Threat Intelligence Report: 2026 Midyear Edition tracked 21,667 vulnerability disclosures during the first half of 2026, an 8% increase.

    Of those, 4,015, or around 19 percent, already had public or functional exploit code. Flashpoint also reported a 45 percent increase in Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) attacks during the period.

    The patent was granted August 11 2026, although the underlying Ransomware Risk model isn't new. It has been available through Flashpoint Vulnerability Intelligence since 2022.

    The model addresses a basic vulnerability-management problem: severity and real-world ransomware risk aren't necessarily the same thing, because severity scores do not necessarily indicate which flaws attackers are most likely to target.

    It has been revealed that the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, or CVSS, measures how severe a vulnerability could be. The Exploit Prediction Scoring System, or EPSS, estimates the probability of exploitation more broadly.

    Flashpoint's Ransomware Risk model adds another dimension by comparing newly disclosed vulnerabilities with the characteristics of flaws previously exploited in ransomware attacks.

    It has been revealed that that could change where a vulnerability lands in an organization's patching queue. A lower-severity flaw might normally sit behind numerous critical vulnerabilities. But if its characteristics closely resemble vulnerabilities repeatedly targeted by ransomware operators, security teams may have reason to move it higher.

    "A severity score alone can't tell you which vulnerabilities pose the greatest real-world risk of exploitation by ransomware actors," Flashpoint CEO Josh Lefkowitz mentioned. "Our patented Ransomware Risk model applies years of threat intelligence to that problem, giving customers an earlier signal and helping them prioritize based on how attackers actually operate.".

    In a recent development, the firm's midyear research also illustrates the scale of the prioritization problem. Its vulnerability intelligence covers traditional IT systems as well as cloud, IoT, operational technology, open source software. and third-party libraries.

    The company notes it also tracks more than 105,000 vulnerabilities that aren't represented in CVE or the National Vulnerability Database, expanding the pool of flaws that security teams may need to evaluate.

    The cybersecurity tech giant's patented methodology profiles vulnerabilities using more than 60 technical characteristics, including whether a flaw can be exploited remotely without authentication, whether it affects operational technology systems, and how exploitation could affect data availability.

    According to recent reports, those characteristics form a multi-factor fingerprint. The model maps each vulnerability against clusters containing flaws previously exploited in ransomware attacks and assigns a Low, Medium, High, or Critical Ransomware Risk rating.

    Sources indicate that flashpoint says the rating can be generated when a vulnerability is disclosed, rather than requiring security teams to wait for public evidence of active exploitation. Ratings are then updated as newly introduced ransomware activity and threat intelligence emerge.

    Within Flashpoint Ignite, Ransomware Risk appears alongside CVSS, EPSS, Social Risk, and exploit maturity. The idea isn't to replace existing scoring systems, but to give administrators additional information when deciding what to remediate first.

    Nor does a High or Critical Ransomware Risk rating mean a vulnerability will necessarily be exploited. The model measures how closely its characteristics resemble vulnerabilities historically associated with ransomware attacks.

    For security teams facing thousands of potential vulnerabilities, that distinction matters. The flaw carrying the highest severity score isn't necessarily the one that most closely resembles what ransomware operators have historically chosen to attack.

    "Despite being the most popular indicator for priority, we know that severity alone doesn't tell you whether a vulnerability will be exploited or used in ransomware," remarked Ben Haynes, Data Science & Analytics Lead at Flashpoint and co-inventor of the patented methodology.

    "A vulnerability can score low on a traditional severity scale and still share the characteristics we repeatedly see in ransomware attacks.".

    For more information, go to the Flashpoint site.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Heated Rivalry caused such a kerfuffle at the end of 2025 that we all collectively as a society forgot that The Hunting Wives got us all hot and bothered with sexy, covert, queer relationships earlier that summer. The Netflix series is now back for season 2 for more deliciously toxic drama. It’s also back with some fresh characters. Here’s what you need to know about who plays who in The Hunting Wives season 2.

    Recent findings suggest that spoilers for season 1, but unless Katie Lowes and Chrissy Metz’s characters decide to haunt the Hunting Wives in season 2, they won’t be returning. And before we get into the major players, additional fresh cast members on The Hunting Wives season 2 include Cam Gigandet as Gentle John Moffitt, WNBA player Angel Reese as “Trainer Barbie,” and Casey Mills as Nico.

    Brittany Snow plays Sophie O’Neil.

    In the first season, Sophie was a fish out of water after moving from Massachusetts to Texas for her husband’s job. Now, she’s acclimated to Southern living; but her old secrets have been replaced with newly introduced secrets.

    Brittany is a former child/teen actress who followed three years on Guiding Light with a main role on American Dreams. She then starred in John Tucker Must Die and played Amber Von Tussle in the movie adaptation of the musical Hairspray. Not long after came Pitch Perfect and its two sequels. You’ve also seen her in X, Someone Great, Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, and The Night Agent.

    Malin Åkerman plays Margo Banks.

    Margo leads the Hunting Wives, a social group for gun and cocktail-loving women in Texas. She takes Sophie under her wing and seduces her in more ways than one, to the chagrin of some of the other women in the group who feel replaced.

    Many would say that Malin broke out in the pre-DCU superhero film Watchmen. But they haven’t seen 27 Dresses, The Proposal, or The Comeback. You may also know her from Dollface, Billions, that one episode of How I Met Your Mother, Trophy Wife, Children’s Hospital, Rock of Ages, and two episodes of Entourage.

    Evan Jonigkeit plays Graham O’Neil.

    Graham is Sophie’s architect husband.

    Evan played the Marvel comics character Toad in X-Men: Days of Future Past. His other film and television credits include Easy, Bone Tomahawk, Frontier, and Whiskey Tango Foxtrot. If you like The Bear and Girls, you need to watch Jonigkeit as Will in the Starz series Sweetbitter.

    Dermot Mulroney plays Jed Banks.

    Margo’s husband Jed is running for Governor!

    Dermot’s romantic comedy fame precedes him. You’ve seen My Best Friend’s Wedding, The Wedding Date, The Family Stone, and Must Love Dogs. He’s also a cellist who has played in the orchestras of several film scores, and played onscreen in Mozart in the Jungle. On television, he had a short arc on Friends and longer recurring roles on demonstrates like Fresh Girl and Enlightened. He was a regular on Shameless and plays the main character Dom in the Chicago Fire/Med/PD world.

    Brad is the teenage son of a late Hunting Wife named Jill.

    Ferrier’s previous credits include Dirty Laundry, Sweet Tooth, and One Of Us Is Lying.

    Callie is the sheriff’s wife and Margo’s ex-situationship.

    Jaime Ray Newman is set to appear next in the Netflix true crime drama The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey. You also know her from Dopesick, The Magicians, The Punisher, Bates Motel, Wicked City, Drop Dead Diva, Major Crimes, and Veronica Mars. She was also on General Hospital for three years in the 00s.

    Hunter Emery and Karen Rodriguez play Deputy Walter Flynn and Deputy Wanda Salazar.

    The cops investigating various local crimes that may/may not involve the wives.

    Industry observers note that earlier this year, Karen Rodriguez played Janet Ruiz on Spider-Noir. And you know Hunter Emery best as CO Rick Hopper on Orange Is the New Black.

    IG: @itsjusthunteremeryIG: @xkarenxrodriguez.

    Upcoming wife alert? We don’t know much about Nadia.

    Kim Matula was a series regular on The Bold and the Beautiful in the 2010s and was nominated for a Daytime Emmy Award in 2014. She was also a series regular on UnREAL and LA to Vegas. She starred alongside Florence Pugh in the underrated gem Fighting With My Family and also played Jane Curtin in Saturday Night.

    Alex Fitzalan plays Lincoln Trout.

    Lincoln is also a upcoming character this season.

    Alex Fitzalan has, on two separate occasions, been part of a teenage survivalist ensemble series: The Society on Netflix and The Wild on Prime Video. His film credits include 2018’s Slender Man and 2022’s Chevalier. Earlier this year he also turned up on The F Ward and the Netflix adaptation of My Brilliant Career.

    Whoever Chase is, he seems fun!

    It has been revealed that john Stamos is best known for playing Uncle Jesse on Full House and hanging out with the Beach Boys in his spare time. He did also have a main role on General Hospital for years before that. Post-Tanner family, Stamos also starred in ER, Jake in Progress, Grandfathered, Scream Queens, and Big Shot. He has also starred in four musicals on Broadway, and frequently performs at the Hollywood Bowl.

    Dale Dickey plays Zelda Moffitt.

    And whoever Zelda is, she seems fierce.

    Sources indicate that you saw Dickey earlier this year on Widow’s Bay. She is the kind of working actress who’s in everything. Her previous television credits include My Name is Earl, True Blood, Justified, Vice Principals, Claws, A League of Their Own, and Bookie. On the major screen, you’ve seen her in Winter’s Bone, for which she won an Independent Spirit Award, as well as Super 8, Hell or High Water, Palm Springs, and Princess Protection Program.

    Other latest cast members this season include Cam Gigandet as Gentle John Moffitt, WNBA player Angel Reese as “Trainer Barbie,” and Casey Mills as Nico.

    SailPoint Intros New Capabilities to Address Agentic AI Identity Security Challenge

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that AI agents are moving from experiments into everyday enterprise environments, but the security controls around them are not keeping pace, according to enterprise identity security company SailPoint.
    • Sources indicate that that gap could become harder to ignore as organizations give agents more autonomy.
    • Recent findings suggest that sailPoint, which develops identity security and access governance technology for enterprises, is responding with a collection of upcoming identity security capabilities unveiled at its Navigate 2026 conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that AI agents are moving from experiments into everyday enterprise environments, but the security controls around them are not keeping pace, according to enterprise identity security company SailPoint. In its latest Horizons of Identity Security report, SailPoint found that 79% of enterprises already have AI agents running in production, while just 2% have deployed identity security tools specifically designed to govern them.

    Sources indicate that that gap could become harder to ignore as organizations give agents more autonomy. Agents can increasingly access applications, sensitive data, and credentials, and in some cases take actions on a user's behalf, effectively creating a new class of identity that IT and security teams need to manage.

    Recent findings suggest that sailPoint, which develops identity security and access governance technology for enterprises, is responding with a collection of upcoming identity security capabilities unveiled at its Navigate 2026 conference. The tech giant is expanding its Agentic Fabric to discover "shadow AI" agents and provide runtime authorization and controls capable of immediately disabling an agent.

    The organization also introduced what it calls SailPoint Autonomous Agents, specialized AI agents designed to govern other agents. The security agents can monitor runtime activity, intercept threats, and adjust permissions while allowing legitimate agents to continue operating, SailPoint stated.

    The idea reflects one of the challenges created by increasingly autonomous AI systems: Traditional human approval processes may not be fast enough to govern software capable of taking large numbers of actions on its own.

    "The idea that a security admin is going to review and approve access for a group of autonomous agents making 10,000 tool calls a second isn't just outdated — it's a fantasy," SailPoint CTO Chandra Gnanasambandam said.

    Another part of SailPoint's approach focuses on visibility.

    Newly introduced endpoint and browser sensors, along with SIEM and XDR telemetry and non-human identity discovery capabilities, are designed to uncover agents, MCP servers, credentials, tools, and data stores that haven't been brought under an organization's identity program.

    Industry observers note that the company is also introducing Autonomous Identity Security Posture Management, or A-ISPM, which uses identity information from its Atlas platform to identify dormant accounts, orphaned access, shadow administrators, and other potentially risky access paths. Organizations can then revoke access, disable an identity or AI agent, assign an owner or automate enforcement.

    Just-in-Time provisioning is another part of the strategy. Rather than giving people, service accounts, and AI agents permanent access, permissions can be granted when needed and subjected to conditions such as reauthentication or a business justification.

    Sources indicate that capabilities across SailPoint's Agentic Fabric, Human Fabric, and Atlas platforms are beginning to roll out globally. A-ISPM and several other announced features are expected in the firm's fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

    "Autonomous agents are no longer just experimental copilots; they are becoming the primary execution layer of modern enterprises," SailPoint President Matt Mills noted.

    For more information, go to the SailPoint site.

    E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    Recent findings suggest that AI is moving beyond assisting cybercriminals and beginning to operate within live attacks, according to a recent report from Check Point Research. The technology is making sophisticated capabilities faster and more accessible while creating new security risks for businesses deploying their own AI systems.

    It’s been a moment since a show’s had me more locked in than Phony on Hulu, and with just one more episode left, inquiring minds (me) want to know: WHEN IS SEASON 2? And also key: is there even going to be a season 2?

    Recent findings suggest that phony follows high schooler Sonny Cooke, who wakes up in the hospital after a car accident to find that his mom seems...off. For starters, her facial features are ever-so-slightly different—but there’s also the fact that she doesn’t remember their special way of saying “I love you” (three hand squeezes), and the fact that she’s just acting generally weird. Was she swapped out by an imposter? Does Sonny have Capgras syndrome? Is there some sort of alternate reality happening? Hopefully we’ll find out by the end of season 1, but then what? Which brings us to...

    It has been revealed that not yet. But given how freely the cast and creators are talking about a second season (and the fact that the show is pretty popular), it seems likely to get a sophomore pickup.

    Yes...but it’ll also end on a cliffhanger. Creator Nick Paley told Us Weekly “I’m really excited about the cathartic emotionality of the [season 1] cliffhanger. This thing kicks us into the next story in this world because I don’t like constantly depriving people of information. I want this to feel like it means a lot and it feels very key to the characters emotionally. So that cliffhanger does both. Every episode has very massive turns at the end. When you’re telling a mystery, it’s really important to show it to people who don’t know.”.

    Paley told the Los Angeles Times that Phony Season 2 will feature “a whole upcoming story” after the season 1 finale delivers “resolutions and answers.”.

    In a recent development, the majority of Phony Season 1 was filmed from March through May of 2026, and it premiered in October—a pretty short production time. So, if the show follows a similar schedule for season 2 and starts filming this spring, we could be looking at another October premiere.

    Sources indicate that potentially a LOT. Connie Britton, who plays Ellen, told The Wrap, "I think Nick has this thing laid out through probably five or six seasons. He's so clear about what the story is, and so I would be very surprised if he has doesn't have Season 2 all ready to go.".

    In a recent development, white-elephant gift exchanges are fun, but first you have to come up with the perfect gift everyone will want—within the established budget. Need a refresher on the game? Here’s how the chaos unfolds: Everyone brings a present, draws a number, and then, going in order based on which numbers everyone drew, either unwraps a mystery gift or steals one that’s already been revealed.

    Sources indicate that some common caveats are that there’s a cap on steals per item (usually two or three), you can’t immediately steal back what was just swiped, and your turn ends when you open your gift (or exchange it for an already-opened one). The final player gets the power position—and sometimes a last swap—depending on house rules. You might also hear the game called Dirty Santa: same energy, same drama, whether it’s with coworkers or cousins.

    Recent findings suggest that what to bring under, say, $50? (That’s a pretty nice price ceiling.) Go funny but functional, like the stocking stuffers people will actually use. Think cozy comforts, clever kitchen gadgets, mini games, candles that actually smell good, and little indulgences that feel pricier than they are. Skip anything weirdly personal—you want universal hits that sisters, brothers, moms, dads, friends, and coworkers can all fight over with a smile. Bonus points if it’s something you’d happily steal back yourself.

    That’s the general idea. It’s like Secret Santa but evil. The best part of all is that cheap is the way to go. A budget of $50 is more than enough, and there’s a lot of shit out there. So we sorted through it all and found the best white-elephant gifts for your 2026 festivities.

    Since the Owala is the best water bottle of all time, we wouldn’t blame you if you ended up stealing it back for yourself.

    Dysons are nice, sure, but this tiny vacuum is well within any budget. It’s great for cleaning desk spaces, computer keyboards, and more.

    Bean snobs swear this is the best way to make your cuppa.

    The weiner-dog ice-cube tray is absolutely causing some fights this year.

    Look at these cute little Yeti espresso cups! Who wouldn’t be psyched to unwrap these?

    Recent findings suggest that A little twist on a classic novel but focusing on cocktails. What more can we ask for?

    Industry observers note that is a Pura smart fragrance diffuser the perfect white-elephant gift? I think so. By connecting to the Pura app, this clever little device lets you personalize your home scenting experience. Whoever gets this should host next time, because their place will smell sooo good.

    This mini Zen garden will bring balance and serenity to their desk, either at home or at work.

    This fun deck of cards will test out their card-playing skills as well as their music knowledge.

    This notepad has little sayings like “I’m not even trying anymore” for the optimist in your friend group.

    These winter months can be cold. I imagine everyone could use some hand cream right now, especially some really nice hand cream from Salt & Stone.

    If they have a penchant for great breakfast foods, they’ll be all about this mini waffle maker.

    Tech Report: Survey: Most Organizations Are Not Consistently Measuring AI Value Against Costs

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.
    • Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.
    • The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs. The organization's Global AI Pulse Q3 2026 report found that 89% of organizations report measurable value from AI, while just 12% consistently assess that value against costs across the organization.

    Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.

    The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.

    Most organizations have established ways to track AI spending: 61% review costs during project approval, and 59% monitor them once systems are operating.

    Consistently connecting those costs to value remains less common. Beyond the 12% that do so across the organization, another 26% assess value against costs for most initiatives.

    Organizations reporting established AI returns have stronger measurement practices. Among this group, 48% consistently assess value against costs, four times the proportion in the overall survey group.

    Cost-monitoring dashboards are also more common among organizations reporting established returns: 77% use them, compared with 43% of those still experimenting.

    Recent findings suggest that "The organizations seeing a return did the implementation and the transformation properly: guardrails in place, workforce ready, data cleaned up," stated Priya Emmanuel, global head of aIQ at KPMG International. "That is a sequence, not a secret.".

    Organizations are also developing more formal systems to manage AI deployment.

    Fifty-five percent operate a formal AI management layer, which KPMG calls a "harness layer," comprising controls and tools between AI models and business applications.

    It has been revealed that security and identity controls, along with data access controls, were the most common capabilities, each reported by 43% of respondents. Model routing, which determines which model handles a particular task, was reported by 23%.

    Meanwhile, 53% assign accountability for AI-informed decisions to a named executive, the CEO, or an executive committee.

    The proportion reporting significant employee adoption of AI agents rose from 25% in the first quarter to 34% in the third quarter.

    Cybersecurity concerns were more common among organizations with mature AI programs.

    Half of those reporting established AI returns identified cybersecurity as a barrier, compared with roughly one-third of those still experimenting.

    Overall, 86% of respondents said their organizations are adapting their cybersecurity operating models to address AI-accelerated threats.

    The report identifies accountability, operational resilience, and cost management as priorities as AI becomes more embedded in business operations.

    Industry observers note that "Many organizations have made AI models widely available and track their use," noted Swaminathan Chandrasekaran, head of the US AI Center of Excellence at KPMG. "But consumption alone is not a strategy.".

    For the full report, visit the KPMG site.

    Carahsoft has created a upcoming community for K-12 schools and districts designed to help education leaders navigate AI adoption and cyber readiness.

    It has been revealed that AI is moving beyond assisting cybercriminals and beginning to operate within live attacks, according to a recent report from Check Point Research. The technology is making sophisticated capabilities faster and more accessible while creating new security risks for businesses deploying their own AI systems.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When I first heard about the social media concepts of age, height, and swag gaps, I was confused as to how they could possibly threaten established relationships, or generally anyone who was into someone else. After all, these are generally known factors.

    When you meet a newly introduced love interest, there will always be characteristics that reveal themselves over time—that's what dating is. Whether you meet someone in person or online, you generally know what you're getting into. Sure, you can lie on Hinge, but one IRL date should usually sets the facts straight.

    Recent findings suggest that unless you're Pedro Pascal in Materialists or Demi Moore in The Substance, there's not much you can do about age and height gaps. Swag gaps, on the other hand, are a little more amenable. You can become a guy's stylist, educate him on the lingo, spots, and social niceties needed to play on the same aesthetically-pleasing field. It takes brute force, hard work, and someone willing to give you carte blanche with their time and dime, but it is possible to close that gap.

    Industry observers note that what is far more dangerous, explosive, and slow-killing is the aura gap. But what exactly is aura? It’s basically the vibe you give off, from your confidence, to your demeanor, to if you’re warm and personable or cold and short. It’s something you’re born with, not something you can buy. Sure, could you learn social skills and etiquette, of course. You could even pay someone to make you seem like you have good aura online, but the truth will eventually present itself in person. You can manufacture an image, but you can't concoct the energy you bring into a room.

    When we consider aura-gap relationships and their longevity, I suspect the issue is less about understanding someone's faults and more fundamental to a partnership's long-term compatibility.

    According to recent reports, the best long-term example I can think of is my parents. My mom is larger-than-life, extroverted, crass, and will leave most people in ab-clenching laughter. My dad is brilliant, detail-oriented, and gets anything and everything done. While those attributes complement each other wonderfully, it's the indescribable warmth and ferocity the duo exude together that makes them such a good team. Their personalities are different, but their auras are entirely compatible.

    And I think that's where the distinction lies. An aura gap isn't necessarily about one person being louder, funnier, or more charismatic than the other. It's about whether the energy you bring into a relationship is reciprocated, complemented, or quietly diminished.

    In a recent development, bad habits, political and religious differences, and financial compatibility are all big factors on marriage checklists, but aura, to me, is even bigger. You can agree on where to live, how many children to have, and what constitutes an appropriate amount of money to spend on dinner, but what good is all that if the person sitting across from you makes you feel like a less interesting version of yourself?

    Sources indicate that as we date, the question should be: does the person opposite me radiate a consistent energy that not only complements my own, but makes mine better? Aura is my non-negotiable, and frankly, it should be yours, too. I'd rather be with someone who makes me feel more myself than someone who makes me feel like I have to be enough for the both of us.

    📅 21 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (706 w)

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Report: Cyber Attacks Increasingly Exploit Trusted Workplace Tools

    📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that in its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick customers into giving them access to enterprise networks.
    • Ontinue's report notes the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.
    • Recent findings suggest that "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that in its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick customers into giving them access to enterprise networks. Approximately 30% of organizations monitored by the cybersecurity tech giant experienced at least one attempt to impersonate IT support through Microsoft Teams during the first half of 2026. About one in every 990 external Teams contacts revealed signs of someone pretending to be an internal IT worker.

    Ontinue's report notes the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.

    Recent findings suggest that "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits. They rely on trust," Balazs Greksza, director of Advanced Threat Operations at Ontinue, said in the tech giant's announcement.

    Ontinue broke down how a typical attack works: An employee gets an unexpected Teams message or call from someone claiming to work in the organization's IT department. The person warns of a security matter, a software problem or an update that can't wait. Then they walk the employee through opening Windows Quick Assist, installing remote-access software, or running a PowerShell command. Following those steps can hand the attacker control of the employee's computer, often without the employee realizing it.

    The approach is very similar to the Black Basta ransomware group, which helped popularize similar attacks in 2024. Unfortunately, Ontinue found the technique has since been adopted by other cybercriminal groups, including some with no known link to Black Basta.

    Recent findings suggest that some threat agents are also combining tactics. They might first overwhelm an employee's inbox with unwanted e-mails, then reach out through Teams pretending to be IT support offering to fix the problem.

    "Phishing no longer resides solely in your inbox. It has spread across the entire corporate communications environment," said Mika Aalto, co-founder and CEO of Hoxhunt.

    Teams impersonation is only part of the problem. Ontinue also found attackers taking advantage of legitimate Microsoft sign-in processes. Between May and June, researchers identified 10 confirmed device-code phishing compromises across five customer tenants.

    Recent findings suggest that in these attacks, criminals trick employees into completing what appears to be a normal Microsoft authentication process. But doing so can give the attacker access to the employee's account and system without actually breaking their password.

    The report also found attackers using blockchain-based infrastructure to hide malicious activity, accounting for more than 25% of confirmed malicious ClickFix findings.

    Recent findings suggest that "Attackers are no longer looking for gaps in your perimeter. They are looking for the systems your organization already trusts and finding ways to move through them undetected," said Shane Barney, chief information security officer at Keeper Security.

    Industry observers note that the security firm indicates that IT needs to keep a closer eye on unexpected Teams contacts, remote-support requests, suspicious PowerShell activity, and changes to authentication settings. Employees should also confirm sensitive requests through established internal channels, rather than relying on the name or account that appears on their screen.

    Aviv Nahum, co-founder and CEO of Above Security, noted that AI is making these attacks more convincing by helping criminals imitate familiar voices, writing styles, and conversations.

    "The security model therefore must shift from 'does this look real?' to 'can I independently verify that this person is who they claim to be?'" Nahum noted.

    The full Ontinue report can be found here.

    Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.

    E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

    Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a latest Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

    Carahsoft has created a fresh community for K-12 schools and districts designed to help education leaders navigate AI adoption and cyber readiness.

    According to recent reports, AI is moving beyond assisting cybercriminals and beginning to operate within live attacks, according to a recent report from Check Point Research. The technology is making sophisticated capabilities faster and more accessible while creating upcoming security risks for businesses deploying their own AI systems.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity organization Sophos.
    • Separate research from Gartner and Cloud Security Alliance found that 82% of organizations discovered shadow AI agents in their environments during the previous year.
    • According to the security firm, organizations have struggled to identify which AI tools employees use, what information those tools access, and whether their use complies with security policies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity organization Sophos. In a recent product announcement, the company highlighted the growing use of shadow AI, referring to AI tools and agents operating without formal organizational approval or oversight. The security firm cited research indicating that 69% of organizations suspect or have evidence of unauthorized AI use.

    Separate research from Gartner and Cloud Security Alliance found that 82% of organizations discovered shadow AI agents in their environments during the previous year.

    According to the security firm, organizations have struggled to identify which AI tools employees use, what information those tools access, and whether their use complies with security policies.

    "Organizations are adopting AI faster than they can secure it, and most security teams can't answer three basic questions: which AI tools are running, what data is going into them, and whether that activity lines up with policy," noted Kyle Falkenhagen, senior vice president of product management at Sophos.

    The tech giant also cited an IDC projection that the number of AI agents could reach 1.3 billion by 2028.

    Sophos researchers reported observing attackers use AI agents within a customer's network to build and test nearly 80 malware modules.

    The cybersecurity firm unveiled the general availability of Sophos AI Defense, a security offering designed to identify AI tools, monitor their activity, and enforce organizational security policies.

    The product operates through Sophos Fusion, the company's cybersecurity platform, and uses information from devices, networks, identity systems, and browsers.

    According to the company, AI Defense can inspect prompts, uploads, and other AI interactions to identify potentially risky activity and help prevent sensitive data exposure.

    For more information, go to the Sophos site.

    A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

    Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.

    Class CrunchLabs, the suite of free curriculum resources from NASA engineer turned YouTube science communicator Mark Rober, has released its first two courses on YouTube.

    Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network challenges can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a recent study from ControlUp.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (811 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: 12 Things You Should Toss From Your Kitchen ASAP Before Thanksgiving

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It’ll soon be the most key day of the year in the kitchen, so give yourself the gift of space and freedom from clutter by doing a quick purge.
    • “Thanksgiving needs every inch of counter, fridge, and cabinet space you’ve got,” claims Ann Lightfoot, cofounder of DDH Home Organizing & Move Management.
    • “You don’t need a Pinterest-perfect pantry.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’ll soon be the most key day of the year in the kitchen, so give yourself the gift of space and freedom from clutter by doing a quick purge.

    “Thanksgiving needs every inch of counter, fridge, and cabinet space you’ve got,” claims Ann Lightfoot, cofounder of DDH Home Organizing & Move Management. “A short edit beforehand means you can find the baster when you need it, the leftovers have somewhere to go, and you aren’t digging past three broken whisks to reach a serving spoon.”.

    But don’t overdo it! “You don’t need a Pinterest-perfect pantry. You need room to work,” claims Lightfoot. “A full organizing project can easily turn into a weekend of half-finished bins, and that’s the last thing anyone needs in November.”.

    It has been revealed that instead of tearing apart the entire kitchen, focus on the areas and items that will have the most impact. “We always say edit before you organize, and this is the editing part: take things out,” claims Lightfoot. “Do one quick pass, ask whether each item earns its space, and let the rest go. Labels and matching containers can wait until January.”.

    Ahead, here’s what experts say to get rid of ASAP so your kitchen will be ready for cooking and entertaining at Thanksgiving.

    “Spices lose their flavor over time, and stale cinnamon or a two-year-old jar of sage will make itself known in your pie and stuffing,” says Lightfoot. “Check the dates on baking soda, baking powder, and flour too. Toss what’s past its prime and make a shopping list while you’re at it.”.

    Glasses with scratches just don’t look great. “I'm all for mixing vintage and contemporary pieces, but damaged drinking glasses and dishes should go,” claims Kerrie Kelly, NKBA, FASID, CEO and creative director of Kerrie Kelly Studio, and NKBA 2026 National Board Chair. “Holiday entertaining is a wonderful excuse to take inventory and make sure you have enough functional pieces for your guests.”.

    Industry observers note that “Three napkins and a stack of faded plates won't set a beautiful table. Let them go and start fresh,” indicates Nikki Boyd, organizing expert, author of Beautifully Organized, and founder of At Home With Nikki.

    It’s amazing how stuff gets pushed to the back of the fridge, never to be seen again. “Fridge space is prime real estate on Thanksgiving, between the turkey, the sides, and everything guests bring,” claims Lightfoot. “Clear out the half-empty dressings, the jam from last summer, and anything you can’t identify.”.

    Be honest with yourself. “If it hasn't come out for a single holiday in years, it's not waiting for this one,” says Boyd. “Keep heirlooms with stories, and release the rest.”.

    Industry observers note that “Kitchen drawers have a way of collecting multiples of things we rarely need more than one of,” claims Laura Kinsella, founder of Urban OrgaNYze. “Pull out your spatulas, peelers, measuring cups, and all those cooking tools that always seem to get stuck in the drawer. If you're not reaching for them when you're hosting 20 people, chances are you don't need them for a regular weeknight dinner either.”.

    According to recent reports, “Your table is your stage. Burnt down candles and stained runners don't belong on it,” says Boyd.

    Containers that have no lids need to go away ASAP. Ditto for lids that don’t have a container. “Before the holiday leftovers start piling up, take 10 minutes to match your food storage containers with their lids. Get rid of anything that's cracked, warped, or missing its match,” says Kinsella. “There's nothing more frustrating than having a refrigerator full of leftovers and realizing you can't find a single lid that fits!”.

    Sources indicate that that bread maker you haven’t touched lately? The air fryer that’s collecting dust? It’s time to donate them. “Any massive kitchenware item that you haven’t used for the past two to three holiday seasons needs to go,” indicates Amelia Meena, owner of Appleshine, Organization + Design.

    If they’re in bad shape, treat yourself to some fresh ones. “Nonstick pans with a flaking coating and sheet pans warped beyond saving make cooking harder than it has to be,” claims Lightfoot. “If you’ve been meaning to replace one, do it now so you aren’t stuck mid-recipe.”.

    Sources indicate that soy sauce and ketchup packets, plastic forks, extra napkins, and the stack of menus add up swiftly. You’ll want that drawer space for foil, twine, and the meat thermometer, so toss the whole lot into the garbage immediately, states Lightfoot.

    Stained, threadbare towels and thin pot holders aren’t safe for pulling a hot roasting pan out of the oven—plus, raggedy mitts don’t exactly scream “festive.” Pitch thin pot holders and recycle old towels into cleaning rags, then treat yourself to a cute newly introduced set of kitchen linens, says Lightfoot.

    The Coolest Fashion Hub of the ’00s Was in a SoHo Basement

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1387 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon.
    • Rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the name “Winona.” "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom.
    • 163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon. Not unlike Truman Capote and his "swans," Rich welcomed friends such as Kate Moss, Selma Blair, Sofia Coppola, Maya Rudolph, Natasha Lyonne, Parker Posey, and Winona Ryder to his basement office in the brand’s downtown flagship store, documenting fittings and gab sessions with a Polaroid camera. Now, 163 Mercer, a upcoming book from IDEA named for the store’s address, shares stories and photographs of fashion’s golden years just before digital changed everything.

    Rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the name “Winona.” "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom. It sold out on day one, and a second printing followed the next year. The experience left him wanting more creative outlets.

    163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s. She met Rich when Jacobs and Marc Jacobs International president Robert Duffy sent her to the store to pick out a thank-you gift for her professional hospitality at the Mercer Hotel, where Jacobs often stayed.

    According to recent reports, the duo, who are so close that they still speak on the phone every day, began brainstorming a project. "I had the photos of all the other girls, so I knew I wanted to do a book with those pictures," Rich mentioned. They considered wallpaper based on the wall collage or a podcast featuring a different one of the girls per episode, but Cassavetes's film background, including her 2007 directorial debut Broken English, made her the perfect book creative partner. IDEA said yes again.

    In a recent development, they worked at Cassavetes’s Los Angeles apartment, laying out images on her oversized office table. "It's a lot like writing a script, which is why I say I ‘directed’ the book; putting together the layout was like making a movie," she noted. Rich occasionally asked her to add an edited image, and she agreed. "We have similar tastes, and we were open to each other's opinions. He has a cool eye," she added.

    According to recent reports, their bond developed when Cassavetes worked down the street. "My title at the Mercer was director of sales, but I was really a VIP manager. I had a basement office, too," she recalled. Before Latest York's indoor smoking ban in 2003, the two took cigarette breaks indoors. "The logistics helped our friendship, hanging out in each other's offices smoking and having tea.".

    It has been revealed that the book features images of regular visitors plus some who came once or twice, and the women graciously cataloged their memories for it. Don't expect captions throughout; it reads in parts like an IYKYK story asking viewers to figure out who is in the photo. "We didn't caption every Polaroid; they weren't like social media posts," Rich explained.

    Nostalgia for an era before our feeds made the post-Covid years the perfect time for Rich to revisit his mementos. The book should appeal to members of Gen Z who are wondering what they missed before social media, and those in Gen X who are longing for a time that felt authentic, rather than conceived in a marketing strategy.

    Instead of a feed, Rich created an office mood board wall that started with tear sheets and magazine covers of the girls in Marc Jacobs, then added fitting-room Polaroids, which grew more playful, plus newspaper clippings and memorabilia. He likened it to his childhood bedroom, which was covered in Charlie's Angels photos. Cassavetes claims the mood board’s special quality was its esoteric nature. "The wall wasn't for a million people to admire. We had privacy. We had fun because we had more freedom.".

    Recent findings suggest that trust bound everyone involved. Rich knew Moss previously, and Cassavetes knew Sofia and Ryder; Rich met the others on the job. Ryder came into the shop independently, and Rich professed his love of Girl, Interrupted. “’That's a girl's movie,’ she stated, and I said, ‘I'm a girl's movie guy,’” Rich recalled. Ryder's infamous 2001 shoplifting case led to her starring in the brand's spring 2003 campaign, appearing on its "Protect the Skin You're In" T-shirts and wearing Marc Jacobs to court.

    Sources indicate that "Selma didn't know the others,” Rich mentioned. “We hit it off when she tried on the Courrèges–inspired collection. I took Polaroids, sent some to Marc, and kept others. She kept coming in. I introduced her to Kate, Missy, and Frankie Rayder, all of them.”.

    According to recent reports, the mood differed from today's brand-celebrity ecosystem of mutual monetary gain. "It was unpretentious; no one was there to get paid. We were hanging out and having fun. That was the Marc Jacobs spirit: more artsy, less corporate. It was a perfect zeitgeist moment," Cassavetes said.

    In a recent development, case in point: Rich met Hilary Swank before her Oscar win for Boys Don't Cry. "She would come to the store, and I would dress her up for all the pre-Oscar award reveals and events. I put her in a tiered ruffle sundress with a beachy vibe for the Independent Spirit Award in 2000," he recalled.

    Industry observers note that impromptu gatherings were plentiful. Once, Moss, Ryder, and Patric Reeves ended up in the office together. "I stocked my fridge with Sofia champagne cans. They were small but potent," Rich said with a chuckle. An image in the book documents the mini party. Though Polaroids waned in popularity after the brand declared bankruptcy and digital cameras and camera phones arrived, Rich kept a stockpile he used until 2015.

    In a recent development, "Sometimes I wouldn't even recognize Winona because she had a upcoming role, hair color, or style," he stated. "But I met all the boyfriends, watched them get married, pregnant, have babies, and divorce.".

    Industry observers note that getting It girls to wear Marc Jacobs was simple. "Marc's clothes were unbelievable; you didn't have to beg them," remarked Rich, adding that the store's cool yet friendly vibe helped. "I was a massive fan of Marc's, and that radiated to everyone I hired," including bartenders, who made great sales associates because "they knew how to talk to people." A generous clothing allowance, four outfits a season instead of uniforms, fueled employee enthusiasm.

    Recent findings suggest that cassavetes remembers Rich's relaxed styling approach. "He made sure the girls didn't wear the same thing." Rich credits his former boss. "Marc liked everybody's take on his clothes. Winona would change the buttons or redo straps; he loved it.".

    Costume designer June Ambrose's favorite memories include discovering hidden treasures in the basement. "Robert has an incredible eye and instinctively knew what I needed; I could trust him. He understood the woman, the attitude, and the personality behind the clothes," she wrote in an email. "He made me fall in love with Marc Jacobs.".

    Rich also gave his editor and stylist friends early access to sample sales.

    His Marc Jacobs career began when Joe Zee took him to his first runway show for the brand. "I was blown away and marched backstage and asked Marc for a job," Rich said. In 1999, he became store manager, eventually rising to vice president of public relations for retail stores during his tenure.

    Sources indicate that before 163 Mercer became the Marc Jacobs store in 1997, it was once the Tony Shafrazi Gallery, which propelled the careers of Francis Bacon, David LaChapelle, and Keith Haring, for whom Rich once worked. "There was nothing in SoHo; Marc could have picked any space. There was good energy there. Tony would stop in and regret having given the space up," Rich said, noting Jacobs kicked off SoHo’s current designer shopping enclave.

    Recent findings suggest that "The store was so laid-back and a fun, creative safe space. It was also the center of the downtown fashion world at that time," Cassavetes added.

    Rich hints that a third book would move away from SoHo. "We wouldn't just be in the office. Maybe it would be pictures from everywhere.".

These are AI agents deployed within an environment that can access data, use software tools, and make decisions without constant human supervision.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.

    In a recent development, in a firm blog post, Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, outlined how Microsoft intends to use Project Perception to monitor, manage, and contain what it calls "agentic insiders." These are AI agents deployed within an environment that can access data, use software tools, and make decisions without constant human supervision. While they can improve productivity, Microsoft warns that they also introduce security risks, even when they haven't been compromised by an attacker.

    In a recent development, "Agents are unpredictable," Gallot wrote. "They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended, and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised.".

    Recent findings suggest that project Perception was first introduced in July. The platform, which entered public preview Aug. 3, is designed to help security teams respond to increasingly sophisticated cyber threats using AI-powered automation.

    Recent findings suggest that instead of leaning only on traditional security alerts and manual investigations, Project Perception uses three kinds of specialized AI agents working together. Red team agents hunt for possible vulnerabilities, blue team agents look into suspicious activity, and green team agents step in to fix problems and strengthen defenses.

    To spot threats and respond faster, the system pulls in security data from identities, endpoints, cloud environments, applications, and other sources.

    Now Microsoft wants to use those same capabilities on the AI agents already running inside enterprise networks. Project Perception would find those agents, give them identities and permissions, and keep an eye on what they do across different systems. It would also keep assessing the risks that come with their actions.

    Microsoft also described a blueprint for "Guardian Agents," specialized AI agents that supervise other agents and step in when their behavior gets risky. That might mean limiting an agent's permissions or blocking certain actions before they cause harm.

    "Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous," Gallot wrote.

    Recent findings suggest that the initiative also reflects concerns raised by Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in an Oct. 10 essay on AI security.

    Nadella argued that enterprises should treat powerful AI models much like potential insider security risks, particularly when those models can access confidential information or perform critical business operations.

    "We simply can't outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf," Nadella wrote.

    He called for security controls that operate independently of AI models, including restricted permissions, detailed activity logging, and mechanisms that allow administrators to stop an agent's actions.

    "In other words, we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it," Nadella wrote.

    Microsoft admits that watching what AI agents do is only part of the answer. Gallot said that future security tools will also need to show why AI models make the choices they do, not just what actions they end up taking.

    For more information, go to the Microsoft blog.

    Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.
